title: feat(pnm): up to ~20× faster commands on a distant VTA (ssh-style ControlMaster)
body:
> **Draft / WIP** — the feature works and is measured, but see *Not done yet* at the bottom.

## Why

Every `pnm` invocation is a fresh process. Each one re-resolves the VTA and mediator DIDs,
opens a TLS connection per host, authenticates to the mediator and upgrades a WebSocket —
and only then sends the command. None of that survives the process, so the next command
pays for all of it again.

On a local stack that is invisible: a round trip costs microseconds, so the setup is free
and every command looks instant. Against a VTA in another region it is the whole story.

Counted off the reverse proxy's access log, one `pnm acl list` over DIDComm is **12–17 HTTPS
requests**: 6 `did.jsonl` fetches, a mediator challenge and authenticate, a WebSocket
upgrade, an inbox drain, the actual outbound/inbound pair, and several cleanup `DELETE`s.
Because each fresh connection also pays TCP and TLS on top of its request, that is **~23
serialised round trips** — for a command whose useful work is one.

## What it costs today, and with this change

`pnm acl list`, three runs per cell, median. Both arms are the same binary and the same
`docker exec` into one long-lived container, so process startup is in neither number; the
~103 ms exec floor is subtracted. Latency injected with a delaying relay in front of the
stack, so these are propagation delay only — no jitter or loss, which makes them floors.

| RTT | one-shot (`--control-master no`) | multiplexed | removed | **ratio** |
|-----:|-----:|-----:|-----:|-----:|
| 0 ms | 64 ms | 41 ms | 23 ms | **1.6×** |
| 50 ms | 1 378 ms | 107 ms | 1 271 ms | **12.9×** |
| 150 ms | 3 646 ms | 215 ms | 3 431 ms | **17.0×** |
| 300 ms | 6 892 ms | 360 ms | 6 532 ms | **19.1×** |

Both sides are linear in RTT, which is the useful form:

```
one-shot     ≈ 22.8 × RTT
multiplexed  ≈  1.06 × RTT
```

The ratio therefore climbs with distance and approaches **~21×** (22.8 / 1.06) as the
fixed local cost stops mattering: 19.1× is what was measured at 300 ms, not a ceiling.

A multiplexed command costs **one application round trip** — the same thing a trust ping
measures. So the rule needs no RTT estimate at all: **the multiplexed number is your trust
ping**, and everything above it is setup the one-shot CLI redoes every time.

| your trust ping | multiplexed | one-shot today |
|-----:|-----:|-----:|
| 50 ms | 50 ms | ~1.2 s |
| 150 ms | 150 ms | ~3.5 s |
| 300 ms | 300 ms | ~7.0 s |

At 300 ms RTT a twenty-command script goes from over two minutes to about seven seconds.

### Starting the master is ~free

The first command has no master to talk to, so it starts one and then delegates. That costs
about what running the command directly would have, because the master does the setup the
command needed anyway:

| RTT | first command (starts master) | one-shot |
|-----:|-----:|-----:|
| 0 ms | 168 ms | 64 ms |
| 50 ms | 1 432 ms | 1 378 ms |
| 150 ms | 3 638 ms | 3 646 ms |
| 300 ms | 7 044 ms | 6 892 ms |

Which is why the default can be `auto`: nobody has to think about it, and nobody pays to
find out.

## What this adds

```
--control-master no|auto|yes|ask    (default: auto)
--control-persist no|yes|10m|600    (default: 10m)
--control-path <PATH>               (default: per-VTA socket in a private dir)

pnm sidecar serve | status | stop   (ssh -M / -O check / -O exit)
```

Names and semantics follow `ssh_config(5)` so the behaviour transfers. Rarely typed:
`auto` starts a master on demand, the way nobody types `ssh -M`.

The client hands the master its own stdin/stdout/stderr over `SCM_RIGHTS`, so a delegated
command's output is indistinguishable from a direct one — same terminal, same `isatty`,
same colours, same redirection.

## Why it is safe to default on

A master that is missing, stale, wrong-version or unusable is **never an error**. Every
such path falls back to the ordinary one-shot command, so the worst case is exactly
today's behaviour. Verified by killing a master with `SIGKILL` and running the next
command: the stale socket is detected, unlinked, replaced, and the command succeeds.

## Security

The master holds the only copy of the operator's admin private key in memory and will run
any command handed to it, so the socket is the privilege boundary:

- control directory forced to `0700` and ownership-checked; socket `0600`
- a symlinked or foreign-owned control path is refused, which closes the path-swap race
- **peer uid verified on every connection** (`SO_PEERCRED` / `getpeereid`) rather than
  trusting file permissions alone, with no exemption for root
- protocol version checked, so a master left running across an upgrade is refused rather
  than guessed at
- `--control-persist 10m` bounds how long the key stays resident — a security control, not
  just resource hygiene
- `ask` confirms before a master is used or created

## Two details taken from the OpenSSH implementation, not its documentation

1. **The socket is claimed atomically.** Binding a temp path and `link()`ing it into place
   means a second master loses with `EEXIST`. The obvious `unlink()`-then-`bind()` would
   remove a live master's socket, leaving that master running but unreachable while every
   later client silently started another. There is a regression test for this.
2. **Stale sockets are removed by the client, on `ECONNREFUSED` only**, and not at all when
   multiplexing is disabled.

Deliberate divergences from ssh are documented in `control/client.rs`: we spawn a child
rather than forking a thread-bearing tokio process; we confirm on the client's terminal so
`ask` works headless (ssh's askpass silently denies with no `DISPLAY`); we vet the control
path, which ssh does not; we do not exempt root from the peer check; and `yes` means "never
silently fall back" rather than ssh's "be the master".

No OpenSSH code is used — the design is reimplemented in Rust.

## Testing

`cargo test -p pnm-cli` — 104 pass, including the socket race, socket mode, path
sanitisation, symlink refusal and the `ControlPersist` time vocabulary. `clippy` and `fmt`
clean.

Against a live stack: idle timeout evicts the master, `sidecar stop` exits it, a
`SIGKILL`ed master is recovered from, `--control-master no` still runs direct, and the
control socket is `0600` inside a `0700` directory on both macOS and Linux.

## Not done yet

- [ ] `-O stop` (stop-listening) as distinct from `-O exit` — matters less here, where a
      session is one short command rather than a shell
- [ ] config-file keys to match the flags, so a default can be set per VTA
- [ ] review of whether `auto` should be the shipped default or opt-in for a release or two
- [ ] the `ask` prompt is per master, not per command — worth deciding which is wanted

Bumps [trust-tasks-rs](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf) from 0.37.5 to 0.37.12.
Release notes

Sourced from trust-tasks-rs's releases.

trust-tasks-rs-v0.37.12

Added

  • messaging/mux: DID multiplexing at a mediator (messaging/mux/*/0.1) (#1068)

  • feat(messaging/mux): DID multiplexing at a mediator (messaging/mux/*/0.1)

    One authenticated connection (the principal) carries live delivery and pickup for many member DIDs: session attaches bound to one connection's sessionId/muxNonce, and stored grants a member DID signs once. Members sign closed statements (muxAttach, muxGrant, muxRevokeAll) with an embedded Data Integrity proof (proofPurpose authentication), verified in a normative order before any state changes.

    Adds attach, detach, grant, list, update (narrow only), revoke, revoke-all (epoch advance), event (live: ready/attached/detached/refused, incl. the tsp-mux subprotocol) and notice (durable: grantsSuspended, grantsRevoked, grantsExpiring, grantsPresent), with shared definitions in messaging/mux/_shared/0.1/mux.schema.json, stable per-statement refusal codes, the unknown-key suspension rule and replay floors.

    Allowlists eddsa-rdfc-2022 as W3C Data Integrity vocabulary for the casing lint.

  • vta/memory: Versioned writes, tombstones, a change feed and named reads (put/delete/list 0.2, get 0.1) (#1067)

vta/memory 0.1 is an unconditional upsert key/value store: put overwrites with no version, so two writers clobber each other undetected; delete is a hard delete, so another device's cached copy never learns the item is gone; and list returns the whole context with no prefix, paging or change feed.

The new versions apply vta/app-state's semantics to memory, restated per spec so each can be implemented on its own:

  • A per-context write counter (MemoryRecord.version, in the new shared definition vta/_shared/0.1/memory-record) serves both as the optimistic-concurrency token and the sync watermark.
  • put/0.2: optional expectedVersion (0 = create only). A failed precondition is versionConflict, with the current version and value in its details so the loser need not re-read. The response returns version, wasCreated, updatedAt and valueBytes. valueTooLarge carries limitBytes / actualBytes. currentValue is withheld from a caller that may write the context but not read it.
  • delete/0.2: leaves a tombstone, takes an optional positive expectedVersion, and treats deleting nothing as success (existed: false).
  • list/0.2: a snapshot (prefix, cursor/limit, values by default as in 0.1) or a change feed from sinceVersion that includes tombstones, with highWatermark, watermarkTooOld and cursorInvalid.
  • get/0.1 (new): up to 256 named keys, each answered once in items,

title: fix(vtc-client): send_task keeps a refusal's document over a session
body:
## Problem

Through `vtc-mcp`, an operation that needs the person's own step-up could not be answered. `vtc/rooms/community/create` came back as

```
session transport error: forbidden: a passkey gesture bound to this operation is required
```

with no step-up link, although the administrator held an enrolled approver and the community had minted a hand-off (VTI-LNK-125 – 131).

`VtcClient::send_task` documents `VtcError::Refused` over a session, carrying the `trust-task-error` document. It sent through the typed `document` helper, which asks the session for the payload alone and maps a refusal to `VtcError::Session(String)`. The refusal's `details`, including `stepUpHandoff`, were dropped before `vtc-mcp` could build the link. Only the `acl` and `git-ns` paths, which use `dispatch_trust_task_document`, kept it.

## Change

Over a session, `send_task` asks for the reply document and reads it as the HTTPS path reads one:

- a `trust-task-error` is `NotFound` where it carries one of the task's declared codes saying the thing is absent, else `Refused` with the document as received;
- a `trust-task-next-step` is `Parked`;
- a `#response` is its payload.

The typed methods and the HTTPS path are unchanged.

## Testing

- New: `a_session_refusal_keeps_its_document_and_the_step_up_it_carries`, `a_session_reply_is_read_as_the_https_one_is`.
- `cargo test -p vtc-client --features didcomm --lib send::` (10 passed), `cargo test -p vtc-mcp`, and clippy on both with `-D warnings`.
- End to end against a live community over TSP: the same `vtc/rooms/community/create` call now answers `stepUpRequired` with a link; after the wallet approved it, the identical call created the room.
- Not run: the full workspace suite.

title: Automated vetting run: peer and hidden vetting pass end to end, unattended
body:
## Summary

`infra/scripts/vetting-run.sh all` now runs peer vetting, then hidden (PCS) vetting, end to end against the local Docker stack. There is no human in the loop.

**People and services:**
- Four real OpenVTC clients:
  - two vetters, `carol` and `dave`
  - one applicant per flow: `alice-<run>` for peer vetting, `bob-<run>` for hidden vetting
- One real mediator, DID host, VTA and VTC.

**How it is driven:**
- Each client is the production `openvtc` (state handler, VTA session, mediator listeners, inbound handling). `openvtc script …` drives it in place of the TUI. That mode is behind the off-by-default feature `scripted`, in `openvtc/openvtc/src/script_cmd*`.
- The administrator's console steps are scripted with a virtual WebAuthn passkey over the Chrome DevTools Protocol (`infra/bin/console`; no npm packages).

## Verified

Final unattended run: `vetting-run.sh all`, exit 0. The VTC logs show:

- **Peer:** `join request decided under criterion criterion=kernel-developer`. The applicant presented two named Vetting Statements.
- **Hidden:** `hidden-vetting proof verified and counted … criterion=kernel-developer-hidden attestations=2 counted=2`, then `verdict="allow"`. The community counts two distinct vetters without learning who they are.

Tests:
- `openvtc-core`: 1,224 lib tests pass.
- `openvtc`: 1,418 tests pass.
- `cargo check --all-targets` is clean with and without `scripted`.

## Fixes found on the way

These all block any OpenVTC client against a `localhost` stack. Each applies only under `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS`; without it, behaviour is unchanged.

- **Runtime TDK:** the state handler's own TDK resolved with the public-only host policy, so join-status polls could not be packed.
- **Status list:** the client refused a membership credential whose revocation status list is served over http.
- **Manifest:** the client refused to read the community's manifest over http.
- **Mediator:** its Trust Task proof verifier refused the VTC's delivery-status checks. Fixed with a local patch on the same `MEDIATOR_ALLOW_PRIVATE_DID_HOSTS` opt-in. The image now builds in an 8 GB Docker VM.

## Notes for reviewers

- A vetter's client treats a community that hides *any* criterion's vetters as hiding all of them. So the run does named vetting with no hidden criterion present, then adds `kernel-developer-hidden` and turns hidden vetting on.
- The vetters' own admission (`console approve-join`) and their vetter grant (`cnm vetting vetters grant`) are done by the script as the administrator.

All commits are signed, with DCO sign-off.

title: feat!: move to pcreds with Jali 0.3.0 and application contexts
body:
Brings the crate up to the research implementation at
[etairi/predicate-credential-system@5d11dc4](https://github.com/etairi/predicate-credential-system/commit/5d11dc4)
with this repository's adjustments, adds application contexts to its protocol for OpenVTC, and
ports the demo to it. It is breaking (`feat!`), so release-plz will propose 0.2.0.

138 files changed (+45,637 / −28,032), of which the demo is 10 files (+901 / −520).

## The library: `pcreds` replaces `pcs` and `cred`

- **`pcreds`** is the protocol `Π_PCreds` of the paper's revised version, generic over its
  building blocks (`pcreds::Backend`). The modules `pcs` and `cred` are removed.
- **Pairing instantiations:** `Σ-PS` and `Σ-BBS` with `Tag_DDH` and `Tag_DY` over BLS12-381. The
  sigma protocols follow `draft-irtf-cfrg-sigma-protocols-04` and
  `draft-irtf-cfrg-fiat-shamir-04` (SHAKE128 duplex sponge), with the drafts' vectors in
  `kat/ietf/`.
- **Lattice instantiation** (feature `lattice`): `Σ-vSIS` on an NTRU trapdoor with `Tag_LWR`,
  proved with [Jali](https://crates.io/crates/jali) 0.3.0 and `ntru-trapdoor` 0.1.1, both from
  crates.io and pinned exactly. Its proofs are straight-line extractable by default (Katsumata's
  transform). The feature `lattice-plain` selects plain Fiat–Shamir, and the two builds refuse
  each other's parameters and proofs. `lattice-extractable` stays as an alias.
- **Unchanged:** edition 2024, `rust-version = "1.95.0"`, MIT, no default features,
  `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.

## Application contexts (for OpenVTC, not in the paper)

| Party | Binds | Checked with |
|---|---|---|
| Attester | `attest_in_context(.., app)`: `π_att` bound to `app` | `check_attestation_in_context(hvk, id_q, att, app)` |
| Requester | `request_credential_in_context(.., att_apps, ssid, app)`: `π_iss` bound to each attestation's context, in order, and to the request's own `app` | `evaluate_request_in_context(helper, request, ssid, att_apps, app)` |

- Without contexts, every context is the paper's byte for byte, and the known answers are
  unchanged. An empty context is not the same as none.
- Verifiers take the context bytes from their own copy of the public data.
- Tags do not depend on contexts, so one attester counts once for a recipient whatever contexts
  its attestations carry.
- Documented in `docs/design-notes.md` ("Contexts") and `docs/encodings.md`, and tested in
  `tests/application_context.rs` (6 tests, `Σ-PS` and `Σ-BBS`).

## The demo on `pcreds`

`demo/README.md` ("Changes for `pcreds`") has the details. In short:

- **Vetter periods become helper keys.** `pcreds` has no class labels, and identifiers and
  tags are functions of the helper key (`x_0 = H_id(⟨hvk⟩)`, `x_Q = H_req(⟨pp, hvk, id_Q, j_Q⟩)`).
  So the class labels `vetter/<period>` of design §13 C1 become one helper key per period, the
  epoch rotation of §4.3.
  - *Kept:* removal stays cryptographic. A removed vetter gets no credential under the next
    period and cannot attest at all once its last period is dropped. The window of two live
    periods stays, and one vetter still counts once per request.
  - *Given up:* one request can no longer mix periods, which was C1's aim. An application in
    flight completes under its period while that period is live. After the period is dropped,
    the applicant registers again and the vetters refresh their statements without a new
    session, with new tags. Vetters enrol with a fresh key per period (§18.2), so C2's lifelong
    identifier becomes one identifier per member and period.
  - *Considered and not taken:* one long-lived helper key with the period carried only by the
    token labels. It would keep mixing, but a removed vetter's credential would then stay valid
    for good. Removal would rest on token scarcity alone, and a current vetter could hand tokens
    to a removed one so that it counts as a second, distinct vetter.
- **Tokens use one `Σ-PS` key per label.** The `Σ-PS` of `pcreds` signs one scalar, the serial,
  so the label is in the key (the per-month token keys of §5.1).
- **The submission is a `pcreds` credential request** under `ssid = challenge`, bound to every
  statement's metadata and to the proof context. The VTC evaluates it (`N''`) and never answers
  it with a credential. Its helpers use a policy no request meets, so every credential under a
  period's key is a root admission (C4). A statement whose attestation does not verify is now
  `unverified` and simply does not count. Before, one invalid attestation failed the whole proof.
- **Tests:** 14 end-to-end tests, with VTI's own `requirements::evaluate`. Mutation check: each
  of eight VTC defences was disabled in turn, and each time the test that covers it failed.

## CI

- Clippy runs with `--all-features` (the extractable lattice build) and with the plain set.
- Tests run with `--all-features --all-targets` and with `--features lattice-plain`.
- Docs build in both lattice modes with `-D warnings`, and docs.rs gets `serde, jali, lattice`.
- A new `lattice` job runs `quick_end_to_end_k1` and `proofs_are_in_the_mode_of_the_build` in
  release, in both modes, with the same pinned actions.
- Format, no-default-features, MSRV and package are unchanged. The demo is still not built in
  CI.

## Lockfile

- New: `jali` 0.3.0 and `ntru-trapdoor` 0.1.1, with Jali's dependencies `aes` 0.9.4, `cipher`
  0.5.2, `crypto-primes` 0.7.2, `ctr` 0.10.1 and `inout` 0.2.6.
- Upgraded, and shared with the demo's tree: `crypto-bigint` 0.7.5 → 0.7.11 and `ctutils`
  0.4.2 → 0.4.8.
- The demo's pins (`vta-sdk =0.56.1`) and the rest of its tree are unchanged.

## Kept from `main`

- `Cargo.toml`: the MSRV comment, the author note (now naming base commit 5d11dc4),
  `repository`, publishing (no `publish = false`) and `[workspace] members = ["demo"]`.
- `README.md`: the demo link, and the sentence on the crates.io release by release-plz.
- `release-plz.toml`, `RELEASING.md`, `LICENSE` and `publish.yml` are untouched.
- `docs/openvtc-integration.md` comes from the research repository, corrected where its text is
  wrong for this one (the crate is published, and attestations can carry an application
  context), and without the research repository's outdated note on the extraction of the
  proofs.

## Consumers and related work

- VTI's workspace depends on `predicate-credential-system = "0.1"`, so `vti-vetting-pcs`, which
  uses the class labels of `pcs`, stays on 0.1.x until it is ported. That port is the same one
  the demo went through here.
- This supersedes the `post-quantum` branch (two commits on `main`, no PR), which added a
  lattice instantiation to the old API. It can be deleted once this merges.
- #4 (interactive walkthrough) changes the same demo files on the old API, so it needs a port to
  this one after this merges.

## Verification

Run locally on 2026-11-16 (macOS arm64, rustc 1.100.0, the toolchain 1.95.0 for MSRV), on this
tree before it was committed:

| CI step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | pass |
| clippy, `--all-features` and the plain set, `-D warnings` | pass |
| `cargo test --all-features --all-targets` | 400 passed, 0 failed, 24 ignored |
| `cargo test --features lattice-plain` | 415 passed (with 15 doc tests), 0 failed, 24 ignored |
| `cargo build --no-default-features` | pass |
| `cargo doc`, both lattice modes, `-D warnings` | pass |
| MSRV 1.95.0, `cargo check --all-features` | pass |
| `cargo package --locked` | pass (with `--allow-dirty`, as the tree was not committed yet) |
| `lattice` job, four tests in release | 4 passed |
| `cargo test -p pcs-vetting-prototype --release` (not in CI) | 14 passed |

The 24 ignored tests are the heavy lattice suites, which run by hand (README, "Building and
testing").

title: feat(vtc-service)!: serve the landing page from a directory (website.landing_dir)
body:
## Why

A community wanting its own landing page had to either edit `vtc-service/website-default/` and rebuild the daemon, or set `website.root_dir` — which must sit on a separate host, because administrators can deploy into it over the network and it would otherwise ride the console's session cookie.

## What

`[website] landing_dir = "<dir>"`: an operator-placed directory served at the website mount in place of the built-in page, **re-read on every request** — edits show on the next load, no rebuild, no restart, no second host.

- **Same-origin is safe here**: nothing over the network writes it (`/v1/website/*` deploy/file tasks act only on `root_dir`), so it carries the operator's trust — the footing `admin_ui.dir` / `members_dir` already have.
- **Boot check** (fails closed): readable `index.html`, directory and `index.html` not world-writable. The check is now shared with the console/portal directories as `website::paths::check_operator_dir`.
- `root_dir` + `landing_dir` together is refused at config load.
- Paths go through the website safety chain (`canonical_within_root`: no hidden files, no escape incl. symlinks, no exec bit); misses and directory requests fall back to `index.html` as HTML; `Cache-Control: no-cache`; default CSP still applies.
- `vtc website export <dir>` writes the built-in page out as a starting point (refuses a non-empty directory).

## Breaking

- `WebsiteConfig` gains `landing_dir`.
- `routes::router_with` / `router_with_xff` / `assemble_with_website` take `website::WebsiteSource` (`BuiltIn | Landing(PathBuf) | Filesystem(WebsiteState)`) instead of `Option<WebsiteState>`.

## Tests

- Unit: export round-trip + serve from disk + edit picked up; nothing outside the directory / no hidden file served; boot check (missing index, world-writable); config exclusivity and path-mode acceptance.
- Integration: `routing_modes::path_mode_serves_the_landing_dir_beside_the_other_surfaces` — `/` serves the directory, `/health` and `/admin/` keep their surfaces, an edit shows on the next request.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3796 passed. `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. `scripts/check-docs.py` passes.

## Docs

`docs/03-vtc/website-and-admin.md` (*Your own landing page, from a directory*, config block, quick reference, path-mode note), `docs/03-vtc/getting-started.md` step 6, `vtc-service/website-default/README.md`.

title: fix(vta-service)!: a key-role did:webs signs with the key of the proof's purpose
body:
## Problem

A wallet sign-in to a community as a key-role `did:webs` identity is always refused.

A key-role did:webs publishes a different key for each relationship (VTI-KEY-072): its `operational` key under `authentication`, its `attestation` key under `assertionMethod`, and the key event log's own key under neither. A sign-in signs two documents: `auth/oob/identify` for `authentication` and `auth/oob/grant` for `assertionMethod`.

- `vault/sign-trust-task` signed every document with the vault entry's one stored `signingKeyId`, so the community refused one of the two steps whichever key the entry named (VTI-KEY-022). Seen against a live VTC as `carried document proof does not verify` at `prove`, then, with the authentication key entered by hand, `verificationMethod is not listed under assertionMethod in its DID document` at `respond`.
- `vta/dids/list` reported the key event log's key as `signingKeyId`. The browser wallet stores that value in the entry, so the default entry named a method the document lists nowhere.

## Change

- `operations::persona`: `persona_key_for` answers for a key-role did:webs with the role key of the relationship, checked against the identity's own document and held to the same record checks as a level-1 identity. New `role_key_id_for` names that key record where the identity, not the caller, decides the key.
- `operations::vault::sign_trust_task::sign_envelope`: where the principal is a key-role did:webs this agent holds, the proof purpose decides the key. Every other principal still signs with the entry's key. The key is still held to the entry's context (custody rule 7).
- `operations::dids`: the listing reports the `operational` key as `signingKeyId` for a key-role did:webs.

## Breaking

`sign_envelope` takes the persona stores (`PersonaStores`), a signature change in a published crate.

## Testing

- New: `a_key_role_did_webs_is_a_persona_signing_with_the_key_of_the_relationship`, `a_did_webs_without_key_roles_names_no_role_key`.
- Ran `cargo test -p vta-service --lib` filtered to the did:webs persona, DID listing and vault tests: 68 passed.
- Not run: the full workspace suite. Not yet tried end to end against the VTA and VTC where the failure was seen.

## Not in this PR

- The level a key-role identity reports in `vta/dids/list` is still `1`.
- The legacy SIOP `proxy-login` path still uses the entry's stored key.

title: fix(onboarding): reach a did:webs agent's REST endpoint
body:
Onboarding asked `didWebvhDomain` which host to request access to. For a did:webs agent that returns `undefined`, so the wallet asked for no grant, and its first REST call was refused by the browser as CORS with nothing to say why. vta-service's REST layer is origin-allowlisted, so the extension must hold the host permission.

There are two causes, and this fixes both.

1. **The method.** New core `didHost(did)` returns the host a DID names whatever its method: did:webvh, did:webs (first segment), or a did:scid's `src`. A DID that names no host (did:key, did:peer, a bare did:scid) returns nothing. Onboarding's up-front grant and its resume-after-the-permission-dialog path both use it.
2. **The host.** An agent's REST endpoint is not always on its DID's host. A did:webs is published on a shared hosting server, so for one it never is. Once `prepare` has read the agent's document, the view checks the REST base URL's origin. If that origin isn't granted, it shows **Allow access to <host>** on its own click, because the first click's user gesture is spent by then.
   - **Beside a relay** (TSP or DIDComm): the grant is optional, and Connect isn't held back, since REST is then only the fallback.
   - **REST is the only transport:** the grant is required, and Connect stays disabled until it lands, rather than failing as an unexplained CORS refusal.

The setup pane's *agent reachable* check now reads the connection's `restBaseUrl`, which is what the wallet actually fetches, and falls back to the DID's host.

## Tests

- **core** `did.host.mjs`: host per method, a port kept encoded, and no host for did:key, did:peer, a bare did:scid or a did:webs with no AID.
- **render** `onboard-scope`:
  - a did:webs agent's host is requested;
  - a REST origin on another host is offered beside a relay;
  - with REST as the only transport, Connect is held back until the origin is allowed.

`npm test` and `npm run build` pass.

title: fix(vta-service): refuse to sign a document as the did:key of a did:w…
body:
Title
fix(vta-service): refuse to sign a document as the did:key of a did:webvh update key

Body
## What and why

A `did:webvh` the VTA builds uses one key twice: as the DID's signing key and as
the update key that authorizes the DID's log. `keys/sign-document` signed a
caller's document as the `did:key` of any key in the caller's scope, including
that one. A proof by `did:key:<update key>` is exactly what a log entry carries.
So any holder of `sign-document` in the context could have the VTA sign a forged
log entry that adds the caller's own key to the DID. The caller would then
control the DID, and keep that control after its grant is revoked.

`sign-document` now refuses to sign as a `did:key` whose key is an active update
key or pre-rotation key of a `did:webvh` this VTA holds, and answers `Forbidden`.
The same key still signs as the `did:webvh` it serves, whose proofs name that
DID's own verification method, so legitimate signing is unchanged.

title: fix(vta-service): refuse to sign a document as the did:key of a did:w… (#2765)
body:
fix(vta-service): refuse to sign a document as the did:key of a did:w… (#2765)

* fix(vta-service): refuse to sign a document as the did:key of a did:webvh update key

A VTA-built did:webvh uses one key as its signing key and its log's update
key. keys/sign-document signed a caller's document as the did:key of any key in
the caller's scope, so a holder of sign-document in the context could have the
update key sign a forged log entry (a proof by did:key:<update key> is exactly a
log entry's) that adds its own key to the DID, and keep that key after its grant
is revoked.

sign-document now refuses to sign as a did:key whose key is an active update or
pre-rotation key of a did:webvh this VTA holds. The key still signs as the
did:webvh it serves, whose proofs name that DID's own method.

Signed-off-by: Denys Popov <denys.p@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service): read log authority from the did:webvh logs, not the key-handle index

The guard asked the webvh key-handle index whether a key authorizes a
log. That index is bookkeeping, and three of its gaps let a forged entry
through:
- After an update that declares no keys, the previous version's handles
  are superseded and nothing is reinstalled, while the update key stays
  in force.
- DIDs created before the index existed have no handles.
- An update key that is also a verification method is filed under `vm:`.

`did_webvh::log_authority::log_authorized_by` now reads what a verifier
reads. A key is log-authorizing if any entry of a held log names it in
`updateKeys` or commits to its hash in `nextKeyHashes`. Any entry counts,
not only the head, because a proof by an earlier key forks the log. Logs
that do not contain the key or its hash are skipped without parsing. An
unreadable entry fails closed for that DID only, so one bad record
cannot fail every did:key `sign-document` call.

The refusal is `keys/sign-document/0.1` item 6 (a key bound to another
protocol), so it answers `failedPrecondition`, not a bare Forbidden. It
is audited as a key-custody refusal and logged with
`security_alert = true`. The key doubling as update key and verification
method is the VTI-KEY-093 divergence already in the register.

Tests: a metadata-only update, a pre-rotation commitment, and a key the
log lists only as a method (which still signs). The forged-entry test
now asserts the refusal's reason.

title: fix(pcreds): separate empty and absent attestation contexts in π_iss
body:
fix(pcreds): separate empty and absent attestation contexts in π_iss

issuance_context_in appended nothing for att_apps = Some(&[]), the same as
for None, so with no attestations a π_iss proved without application
contexts verified under the context API with an empty att_apps, against the
documented rule that an empty context is not the same as none.

When att_apps is Some, an item att-apps (the number of contexts) now goes
before the att-app items, so Some is distinct from None whatever it holds.
The None encoding is unchanged, so the paper's contexts and the pinned
regression vectors stay as they were. A test covers the zero-attestation
case and fails without the fix.

- vtc: issue_vetter_root rebuilds the enrolment ssid for the submitting
  member instead of taking it from the caller, so a captured root request
  cannot be replayed by another member to lock its owner out of the period

  checks, so an ineligible statement does not burn its token

  attestation (e.g. in refresh) leaves the token reserved and release()
  returns it, instead of losing it

  so the per-period key is only held where it is wiped on drop
- applicant: replace checks the new attestation before dropping the old one
- ci: the self dev-dependency comment now lists jali and lattice too

replace fixes.

title: fix(links): a did:webs community can issue a sign-in link
body:
Reported live: a sign-in link from the SEDI VTC, whose DID is `did:webs:webvh.storm.ws:sedi-vtc:…`, opened the wallet's *Update needed — This code needs a newer version of the app.*

That message is VTI-LNK-021's `update` outcome. It is what a reader must say for a contact DID method it has no resolver for (`unsupported-vid`), and the wallet's contact-method table listed did:webvh, did:web and did:scid only. A test even pinned `did:webs:example.org` as unsupported.

The spec covers did:webs:
- **VTI-LNK-119** names it as a route-A, host-named contact.
- **VTI-LNK-052** has the reader verify its KERI key event log.

`@openvtc/vti-didcomm-js` 0.16 already does this: it verifies every event, signature, pre-rotation commitment and designation, and builds the document from that state, never from `did.json` alone.

## Changes

- **`WEBS_CONTACT_POLICY`**: route A. Well-formed means a host and an AID. The person is shown the host and path, not the AID (`webvh.storm.ws/sedi-vtc`).
- **`WEBS_CONTACT_METHOD`**: runs the existing `assertResolvableWebsHost` egress check first, then the resolver. The document must carry the DID's own id.

## Tests (`did.contact-methods.mjs`, `links.trigger-link.mjs`)

- Acceptance, route and label.
- Resolution, and a document for another id refused.
- A key event log that does not verify → `did-document-unverified`.
- A `localhost%3A8000` host refused before anything is fetched.
- A did:webs with no AID → `bad-from`.

`npm test` and `npm run build` pass.

**Not in this PR:** the onboarding view's host-permission lookups read only a did:webvh agent's host (`didWebvhDomain`). That matters only when onboarding a did:webs agent over REST, which is a separate fix.

title: feat(vtc-mcp): several communities from one --listen bridge (--communities)
body:
## What

`vtc-mcp --listen <addr> --communities <file>` bridges every community a TOML file names from one process, each at `/mcp/<name>` as its own identity, policy, audit log and wallet sign-in. Only the port and the bearer token are shared; nothing is served at `/mcp`.

```toml
[community.first-vtc]
vtc_did        = "did:webvh:…:vtc.example.com"
agent_key_file = "keys/first-vtc.json"   # owner-only; the --mint-did-key JSON
confirm        = "sensitive"
audit_log      = "first-vtc-audit.jsonl"

[community.acme]
vtc_did            = "did:webvh:…:acme.example"
agent_secrets_file = "~/.config/vtc-mcp/acme-persona.json"
read_only          = true
```

## Why a path per community, not a `community` argument

Design note D7a. Each MCP server a host sees stays one identity at one community: a host's approval of one server's tools is never an approval at another, one guard never answers for several communities, and the tools, prompts, workflows and skill are unchanged. Each path has its own MCP session manager, so a session from one community's endpoint is refused at another's.

## Rules

- **Fatal (policy):** unreadable file, unknown key (`deny_unknown_fields`), bad name, bad confirm level / transport, audit log that cannot be opened, **one agent DID for two communities** (VTI-KEY-005, VTI-KEY-006 — the reuse note warns for a single bridge; a file naming both can refuse).
- **Degrades one community (identity):** key file missing, unparseable, readable by others, or not the `agent_did` beside it.
- Key material never in the TOML; the DID is derived from the key.
- Policy flags beside `--communities` are defaults; a section's `deny` adds to `--deny`, never lifts it. `--vtc-did`, `--vtc-url`, identity flags and `--audit-log` are refused beside it; `--communities` requires `--listen`.
- Communities connect concurrently; log lines and `vtc_status` / `vtc_whoami` carry the community name.
- stdio and single-community `--listen` unchanged; `vti_mcp_common::listen::{router, serve}` keep their signatures, so `vta-mcp` is untouched.

## Changes

- `vti-mcp-common/src/listen.rs`: `router_many`, `serve_many`, `mcp_path_for`, `check_service_name`
- `vtc-mcp/src/communities.rs` (new): the file loader
- `vtc-mcp/src/main.rs`: one `open()` per community, shared by both paths; `--communities`
- `vtc-mcp/src/server.rs`: `BridgeIdentity.community`, in status and call logs
- Docs: operator page §7.2, design note D7a + rollout row 9, crate `CLAUDE.md`

## Testing

- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-mcp -p vti-mcp-common -p vta-mcp`: 111 passed, including two communities on one port each reporting its own identity and policy, path isolation and cross-session refusal in `vti-mcp-common`, and the loader's fatal / degraded split
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-mcp -p vti-mcp-common -p vta-mcp --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, `scripts/check-docs.py`: clean
- Binary smoke test with two unreachable communities: `/mcp/alpha` and `/mcp/beta` answer `initialize` 200, `/mcp` 404, both degrade independently, a shared key and a conflicting flag are refused, clean shutdown
- Not yet run: the full workspace suite; a live community (migrating the author's own bridge next)

title: feat(vtc-service): serve vtc/storage/credentials/recipient/0.1 so the console seals for any DID method
body:
The admin console couldn't seal a storage credential for a **did:webs** community. A **did:webvh** community on a DID host had the same problem. The console read the community key only from the same-origin `/.well-known/did.jsonl`, which neither of them serves.

The VTC now serves **`vtc/storage/credentials/recipient/0.1`** (spec trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1329, pinned in `vti-specs-vtc`), and the console asks it for the key instead of reading the log.

**Community (`trust_tasks::storage_tasks`)**
- **Authority:** requires `vtc.rooms.admin` (item 1).
- **Answer:** the Ed25519 key `SealedCredentials` opens with, as a `did:key`, and the verification method that publishes it (item 2).
- **Rotation check:** when its own DID resolves, the answer is checked against the document. If the document publishes a different signing key, it refuses with `notPublished` (`retryable: true`) and carries no key (item 3). If its DID doesn't resolve within 5 s, it answers from the key it holds, as item 3 allows.

**Console (`admin-ui/src/lib/sealed-transfer.ts`)**
- Accepts the answer only when it names the community's own DID and a verification method under that DID (item 4), then seals to `recipientKey` (item 5).
- A `notPublished` refusal is shown as the reason, with the `cnm` command beside it. Other refusals pass through unchanged.

**SDK and `cnm`**
- New `vta_sdk::node_keys::ed25519_public_key` reads a verification method's Ed25519 key as multibase or as an OKP JWK, which is how a did:webs publishes keys (VTI-KEY-150).
- `cnm storage credentials set` now uses that function in place of its own copy. It still seals from its own resolution, as item 6 allows.

**Registered with the censuses:** conformance witness, error-code witness, `DISPATCHED_WITHOUT_PROOF` entry with the reason, admin-UI manifest, MCP guard verb (`recipient` counts as a read), OpenAPI wrapper with a regenerated snapshot and `wire.ts`.

**Tests**
- New in `room_storage_auth.rs`: a did:webs community resolving to a JWK key answers with the key it opens with; a document publishing another key gets `notPublished`; an unresolvable DID gets an answer from the community's own record; a stranger gets `permissionDenied`.
- `vta-sdk`: reads the key from both multibase and JWK.
- Console: vitest for the new key path, plus the updated Storage page test.

**Local runs**
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: full suite run before the final fixes (6 failures: four censuses and two of the new tests). After the fixes I re-ran only the affected subset (the new tests, census, conformance, spine-proof): 48 passed.
- Workspace nextest excluding the VTC: 7595 of 7596 passed. The one failure was the MCP guard census; after adding the verb, `-p vti-mcp-common` passes.
- Clippy with `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `scripts/check-docs.py` pass. Doctests ran only for `vta-sdk` and `cnm-cli`.
- Console: all 1,623 vitest tests, `tsc`, and `wire:check`.

title: feat(vta)!: every DID the VTA holds through one method-neutral surface (vta/dids/*)
body:
Implements `docs/05-design-notes/did-management.md` (#2761) against the specifications in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1332 (merged, deployed). Also fixes the reported bug **`pnm contexts delete` ignores the context's did:webs DIDs and leaves them published**.

## The problem

Every "which DIDs does this agent hold" question was asked one method at a time, and every caller asked only the methods it knew. Against a VTA whose identities were all did:webs, `pnm did-mgmt dids list` said *No WebVH DIDs found* and the wallet's pickers were empty. Inside the VTA the methods had drifted on rules that are not about the method at all.

## What changes

**Engines** (`operations/dids`). One `DidEngine` per kind of authority: the webvh log engine (did:webvh and its did:scid:vh:1 form), the KERI engine (did:webs), and the key engine (did:key identities this VTA minted, read from their key records). One listing, get and methods answer sit over them.

**Wire**
- Serves `vta/dids/{list,get,methods/list}/0.1`. Retires `vta/webvh/dids/list/1.0` and `vta/webs/dids/list/0.1`.
- `vta/contexts/update-did/1.2`: a string DID must be an identity this VTA holds in that context (`notHeld`), of a class that may be its identity (`didClassConflict`, VTI-KEY-193).
- `vta/contexts/delete/1.2` and `preview-delete/2.0` fix the reported bug:
  - **Preview**: `dids` lists every method's DIDs, so the confirmation names the did:webs.
  - **NotEmpty**: counts them.
  - **Deletion**: ends each did:webs on its host through the same path `vta/webs/dids/delete` takes (`ContextWebsSettler`): the deactivation is published, then the slot removed. Host copies are settled before anything local goes, under the same `hostCleanupFailed` / `abandonHostCopies` rules did:webvh has. An unconfirmed did:webs refuses the deletion or is reported in `daemonCleanupErrors`; it is never dropped unseen.
  - **Spec**: 1.1 named did:webvh only, while forbidding exactly this outcome for did:webvh. 1.2 makes it method-neutral rather than this being a code-only fix.
  - **Offline**: the break-glass `vta contexts delete` has no hosting client, so it reports each did:webs as an unconfirmed copy instead of silently purging it.

**One rule each where the methods had drifted**
- **webvh create**: no longer repoints the context holding this VTA's own identity. A did:webs create always refused this.
- **webvh get, realign and delete**: answer NotFound for an unreachable DID, as their specifications already declared. They answered Forbidden, which confirms the DID exists.
- **webs delete**: refuses a DID that a context still acts as, as webvh delete does.
- **Host reconcile and retire-orphan**: now see did:webs slots. They read them as host-only orphans, which retire-orphan could remove.
- **KeyMint refusal**: names DID creation, not `webvh/dids/create`.

**SDK and CLIs**
- **vta-sdk** `client/dids.rs`: `list_dids` (reads to the end), `get_did`, `did_methods`. `list_dids_webvh` and `list_dids_webs` are removed.
- **pnm `did-mgmt dids list` / `get`**: method-neutral, with a `--method` filter.
- **pnm `did-mgmt dids methods`**: new.
- **pnm `webs list`**: the same listing, narrowed to did:webs.
- **pnm address book and server-delete dependents**: read every method.

## Breaking

- The retired list tasks are gone.
- `DeleteContextPreviewResultBody.webvh_dids` is now `dids`.
- Context tasks move to update-did 1.2, delete 1.2 and preview-delete 2.0.

Nothing is deployed, so the wallet (OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin) cuts over with this release.

## Known remaining path

`vta/contexts/update/1.0` (super-admin) can still set a context's `did` unchecked. `update-did/1.2` is where the check lives; the mock-VTA blocker test now creates its "outside context acts as this DID" state through that path, because such records still exist. Closing it needs `contexts/update` to drop `did` in a new version, which belongs in its own change.

## Tests

- **Engines**: did:key from its own record only; context reach (absent and unreachable answer alike); a no-context identity for unrestricted callers only; every engine in one sorted listing; filters; `context_dids`; `for_did`; the class guard.
- **did:webs end to end**:
  - summarised beside other methods, and not found from another context;
  - **context delete ends it and removes its slot**, with the preview naming it and NotEmpty counting it;
  - a refusing host holds the deletion unless the copy is abandoned, and then it is reported;
  - a persona DID cannot become a node-identity context's DID (`didClassConflict`).
- **`update-did` `notHeld`**: for an unknown DID and for one held in another context.
- **Reconcile**: a did:webs slot is held.
- **Conformance**: witnesses for the new tasks, with summaries built by the engines.

`cargo test --workspace` passes, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.

title: feat(vta)!: every DID the VTA holds through one method-neutral surface (vta/dids/*) (#2763)
body:
feat(vta)!: every DID the VTA holds through one method-neutral surface (vta/dids/*) (#2763)

* feat(vta)!: every DID the VTA holds through one method-neutral surface (vta/dids/*)

Design: docs/05-design-notes/did-management.md. Specification:
trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1332.

Engines (operations/dids): a DidEngine per kind of authority — the webvh
log engine (did:webvh and its did:scid:vh:1 form), the KERI engine
(did:webs), the key engine (the did:key identities this VTA minted, from
their key records) — and one listing, get and methods answer over them.

Wire:
- serve vta/dids/{list,get,methods/list}/0.1; vta/webvh/dids/list/1.0 and
  vta/webs/dids/list/0.1 are retired and no longer served.
- vta/contexts/update-did/1.2: a string DID must be an identity this VTA
  holds in that context (notHeld) of a class that may be its identity
  (didClassConflict, VTI-KEY-193).
- vta/contexts/delete/1.2 and preview-delete/2.0: a context's did:webs DIDs
  are ended on their host (deactivation published, slot removed) through
  the same path vta/webs/dids/delete takes, under the same
  hostCleanupFailed / abandonHostCopies rules as did:webvh, and the
  preview and the notEmpty count name every method's DIDs. Before, a
  did:webs record was purged and its key event log left published as a
  live identity, with nothing reporting it.

One rule each where the methods had drifted:
- a did:webvh create no longer repoints the context holding this VTA's own
  identity (a did:webs create always refused that);
- webvh get, realign and delete answer NotFound for a DID in a context the
  caller cannot reach, as their specifications declare;
- a did:webs delete refuses a DID a context still acts as;
- host reconcile and retire-orphan see did:webs slots, which they read as
  host-only orphans;
- the KeyMint refusal names DID creation rather than webvh/dids/create.

vta-sdk: client/dids.rs (list_dids reads to the end, get_did, did_methods);
list_dids_webvh and list_dids_webs removed. pnm: did-mgmt dids list/get
are method-neutral (--method filter), did-mgmt dids methods is new, webs
list is the same listing narrowed to did:webs, and the address book and
server-delete dependents read every method.

BREAKING CHANGE: the retired list tasks are gone and the context tasks
move to update-did 1.2, delete 1.2 and preview-delete 2.0
(DeleteContextPreviewResultBody.webvh_dids is now dids). The wallet cuts
over with this release.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta): no unused mut in context deletion without the webs feature

vtc-service builds vta-service with webvh and without webs, where the host
settlement's failures are never extended.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

Coordinated OpenVTC release Banyan — a known-good, cross-project snapshot of all OpenVTC projects. Tagged at the main-branch HEAD on 2026-06-23.

Changelog

Sourced from dtg-credentials's changelog.

[0.14.0] - 2026-11-10

Breaking: a VAC states purposes of use (DTG Core Credentials, context v2), and verify_chain holds a chain to them — see Changed (breaking) below.

Added

  • A VAC states purposes of use (DTG Core Credentials, Purposes of Use; trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#84). credentialSubject.purposes is optional, {"scope":"any"} or {"scope":"listed","purposes":[...]} with a non-empty list of registered names or absolute IRIs, each once; absent means any, and any never grants modelTraining. dtg_credentials::purposes::PurposeScope models it, read strictly (an any carrying purposes, an empty list or a duplicate is refused at parse). A VAC stating it lists DTG_CONTEXT_V2 (https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/context/v2) second, which is now recognized beside v1; a VAC stating it under v1 is refused.
  • verify_chain enforces the chain rule and reports the effective purposes. A link stating none takes its parent's; a link stating purposes its parent does not grant is AuthorityError::WidensPurposes. The root states the grant, so only a root naming modelTraining can pass it on. VerifiedAuthority::purposes carries the result.
  • DTGCredential::with_purposes states them (switching the context to v2), and with_purposes_under refuses at issue purposes wider than those the parent states.

Changed (breaking)

  • CredentialSubjectAuthority gains purposes, VerifiedAuthority gains purposes, and AuthorityError gains WidensPurposes; DTGCredentialError gains InvalidPurposes (non-exhaustive).

  • did:scid parties are matched by their DID. Chain verification (verify_chain, delegation chains) and the acknowledgement/acceptance pairing compare an issuer, subject, presenter, governing party or principal by DID, ignoring a did:scid ?src= locator (VTI-KEY-160): did:scid:vh:1:<scid>?src=a.example and did:scid:vh:1:<scid> are one party. A did:scid and its did:webvh log are still two. Every other DID compares as before. A proof's verificationMethod is still bound to its issuer exactly.

  • Depends on affinidi-did-common directly (already in the graph through affinidi-data-integrity).

Security

  • DTGCredential::verify_proof_with_public_key now refuses a proof that was not made by a key of the credential's issuer. It verified the signature under the key it was handed but never checked that the proof's verificationMethod belongs to issuer, so a caller that resolved the method the proof names and then trusted issuer() accepted a credential naming any issuer, signed by anyone. It now returns DTGCredentialError::ProofNotFromIssuer, as verify_grant_with_public_key already did; the two share one check. A method belongs to the issuer when the DID before its # is exactly the issuer, when it is the issuer itself, or when it is a bare #fragment (read against the issuer — verify_grant_with_public_key previously refused that form). The comparison is verbatim. A caller signing with a key whose id is not a method of the issuer will now see its own credentials refused; give the signing secret the issuer's method id.

title: ci: compare PR checks with the merge commit's base, not the stale pull_request.base.sha
body:
`github.event.pull_request.base.sha` stays at the commit a PR branched from. The jobs, however, check out GitHub's merge commit, which contains the *current* base. Once a Release PR merges, every open PR that predates it is blamed for that release's version bumps. #1324 failed **versions change only in the Release PR** with 12 `version changed` errors, from #1321 and #1326, although it changes no version.

All seven uses of `base.sha` (version edits, spec lifecycle, published schemas, and the Rust/TS/Go/Dart API-compat jobs) now use `HEAD^1`, the base the merge commit was built on. Every job already checks out with `fetch-depth: 0` and on the merge commit.

**Checked locally** by merging #1324 onto main and running the scripts:
- `VERSION_BASE_REF=e9d913cad` (the old `base.sha`) reproduces the 12 errors.
- `VERSION_BASE_REF=HEAD^1`: `No version declaration changed`.
- With `HEAD^1`, `check-published-schemas` and `check-spec-lifecycle` also pass.

The API-compat jobs use `BASE_REF` only for the `<last tag>..BASE_REF` history and a `git diff BASE_REF HEAD`. `HEAD^1` is the more accurate value there too, and I haven't exercised those jobs end to end.

- **Go** — `verify-go` builds, vets and tests, then `publish-go` pushes the

title: feat(vtc/storage/credentials/recipient): add vtc/storage/credentials/recipient/0.1
body:
Adds **`vtc/storage/credentials/recipient/0.1`**. It returns the key that a [`vtc/storage/credentials/set`](specs/vtc/storage/credentials/set/0.3/spec.md) sealed block is sealed to: the Ed25519 key the community opens with, as a `did:key`, plus the absolute ID of the verification method that publishes it in the community's DID document.

**Why:** a client that can't resolve and verify the community's DID has no way to seal a credential to it. The VTI admin console runs in a browser and reads the community key only from the same-origin `/.well-known/did.jsonl`:
- a did:webs community never serves that file, so the console fails every time;
- for a hosted did:webvh, the console would have to fetch and verify a log from another origin;
- for a did:webs, it would have to verify a KERI event stream.

With this task the key comes over the same authenticated channel the credential then travels on, and it works the same for every DID method.

**What the spec requires:**
- `vtc.rooms.admin`, the same authority `credentials/set` requires.
- The community returns only the key it actually opens with.
- `notPublished` (retryable) when that key is no longer the signing key its document publishes, so nothing gets sealed to a key that has rotated away.
- The client accepts the answer only from the community it addressed, and seals only to `recipientKey`.
- A client that resolves the DID itself may seal from its own resolution. It should refuse to seal if this task's answer names a different key.

Also changes `credentials/set/0.3`, prose only: the sealed-block definition and the `related` list now point to the new task.

Bindings were regenerated for all four libraries. `npm run check` passes, and the Rust conformance tests for the new module pass.

Consumer: VTI (the VTC serves the task; the admin console and `cnm` use it).

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.40.4
body:
### Added

- **vta/dids**: List, get and methods for every identity a VTA holds; method-neutral context deletion ([#1332](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1332))

A VTA holds identities of several methods, and the only way to ask which
  was once per method: vta/webvh/dids/list, vta/webs/dids/list. Every client
  asked only the methods it knew about, so a VTA whose identities were all
  did:webs reported none, and a new method would add a question to every
  client.

  - vta/dids/_shared/0.2: CONVENTIONS §20 (every identity: which are
    summarised, who sees what, the summary, methods), DidSummary and
    MethodInfo, a did:key profile, and a Summary details heading in each
    profile. §3.1's level-1 refusal is scoped to the key-role tasks.
  - vta/dids/list/0.1, get/0.1, methods/list/0.1.
  - vta/contexts/update-did/1.2: the DID must be one the VTA holds in that
    context (notHeld), and its class may be the context's (didClassConflict).
  - vta/contexts/delete/1.2: every DID in the subtree is deleted as its
    method's delete task deletes it, host work settled first. 1.1 named
    did:webvh only, so a did:webs record was removed while its key event log
    stayed published as a live identity.
  - vta/contexts/preview-delete/2.0: `dids` (every method) replaces
    `webvhDids`, which left did:webs out of the confirmation.
  - vta/webvh/dids/list/1.0 and vta/webs/dids/list/0.1 retired in favour of
    vta/dids/list/0.1.

  Bindings regenerated for all four languages.

- **vtc/storage/credentials/recipient**: Add vtc/storage/credentials/recipient/0.1 ([#1329](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1329))

A room-hosting administrator's client asks the community for the key a
  vtc/storage/credentials/set sealed block is sealed to: the Ed25519 key it
  opens with, as its did:key, and the verification method in its DID
  document that publishes it.

  A client that cannot resolve and verify the community's DID could not
  seal at all. A browser console reading a did:webs would need KERI
  verification, and a hosted did:webvh would need a log from another
  origin. The VTC console read only the same-origin did.jsonl, which a
  did:webs community never serves. The answer comes over the same
  authenticated channel the credential then goes over, and is the same
  for every DID method. `notPublished` covers a key the community's
  document no longer lists, so nothing is sealed past a rotation.

  credentials/set 0.3's sealed-block definition and `related` now point
  at it (prose only).

title: feat!: list every DID the agent holds, whatever its method (vta/dids/*)
body:
Against an agent whose identities were all did:webs, every DID question in this wallet came back empty: the vault's persona picker (*Context "vta" has no DIDs*), the console's DIDs pane, and every offscreen lookup. Each asked `vta/webvh/dids/list`, which answers for did:webvh only. A stopgap that also asked the webs list would have needed a third question for a third method, so this uses the method-neutral family instead. Design: VTI `docs/05-design-notes/did-management.md`. Spec: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1332 (merged). Agent side: OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2763.

## Changes

- **core** — `vta/dids.ts`:
  - `didsList`, read to the end of its cursor through `collectPages`, plus `didsGet` and `didMethodsList`, typed on `TaskParty`.
  - `vtaListDids` and `webvhDidList` are gone with the retired tasks.
  - Admin `contextPreviewDelete` returns 2.0's `dids` (every method).
- **Pins**:
  - Added: `vta/dids/{list,get,methods/list}/0.1`.
  - Moved: `vta/contexts/update-did` 1.2, `delete` 1.2, `preview-delete` 2.0.
  - Unpinned: `vta/webvh/dids/list`.
- **Offscreen lookups** list through `didsList`: elections, directory, sign-in personas, `bindProfile`, the community identity check and the vault picker.
- **Vault form**: takes the agent's own `signingKeyId` from the summary rather than resolving the DID document. For a did:webs, a verification-method id is not the agent's key id, so a did:webs persona entry now names a key the agent can sign with.
- **Console**:
  - **DIDs pane**: one table with a Method column. A did:webvh row keeps its log, realign and delete; a did:webs or did:key row opens a read-only summary.
  - **Pickers**: the contexts, persona and room pickers list every method.
  - **Room signing key**: matched by the summary's `signingKeyId` as well as the `did#` prefix, which a did:webs key id does not carry.
  - **Context-deletion preview**: names every method's DIDs.
- **CLAUDE.md**: new section, *DIDs are listed method-neutrally*.
- **task-surface.json**: resynced from the vta-sdk on #2763; coverage 245 → 247.

## Breaking

title: chore(deps)!: take vta-sdk 0.74, affinidi-tdk 0.33, messaging-sdk 0.41, trust-tasks 0.35 and trql-client 0.29; release 0.26.0
body:
Moves VGI onto the VTI #2300 line so openvtc (OpenVTC/openvtc#512) keeps a single `vta-sdk`: `vta-sdk` 0.74, `affinidi-tdk` 0.33, `affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.41, `trust-tasks-rs`/`-proof` 0.35, `trql-client` 0.29, and test mediator 0.46. The workspace and its internal pins go to **0.26.0**, as do `bridge.example.toml` and the tag `v0.26.0`.

## ⚠️ Draft: waiting on trql-client 0.29

`trql-client` 0.29 comes from affinidi/affinidi-trust-registry-rs#172 and the registry release after it, and isn't on crates.io yet. **`Cargo.lock` isn't updated in this commit**, because it can't resolve until then. Once 0.29 is published I'll run `cargo update`, commit the lockfile, and mark this ready.

## Changes

- **Registry test fakes answer `registry/authorization/0.2`.** trql-client 0.29 asks at 0.2 (lowerCamelCase: `entityId`, `authorityId`, `evaluatedAt`) first and falls back to 0.1 only on `unsupportedVersion`. The fakes in verify-trust and vgi-bridge answered 0.1 snake_case, which 0.29 refuses as a contract violation. That caused 4 verify-trust test failures before this change.
- **`#[allow(deprecated)]` for trust-tasks-rs 0.35's prebuilt spec modules.** vgi-bridge allows it at crate level, plus three test files. Its `git-ns/bridge/{job,result,event}` types come from those modules. In did-git-sign it covers `print_session_health`, because vta-sdk's `health/details` answer comes from them too. The real fix is generating those types with `trust-tasks-build`, as openvtc now does. That's a follow-up; this PR is a dependency move.

## Checks

These were run against the registry branch, patched in through an untracked `.cargo/config.toml`:

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` is clean.
- `cargo test --workspace --all-features`: 842 pass, 0 fail.
- `cargo fmt --check` passes.
- `cargo tree` has one copy each of `vta-sdk`, `trust-tasks-rs`, `affinidi-tdk` and `affinidi-messaging-sdk`.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no client change
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1)
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4)
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5)
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6)
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): registry queries go out as 0.2 via trql-client 0.29; fakes updated
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*)
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1)
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: `allow(deprecated)` above, until generated specs

title: feat(vta/dids): list, get and methods for every identity a VTA holds; method-neutral context deletion
body:
## Why

A VTA holds identities of several methods, and the only way to ask which was once per method: `vta/webvh/dids/list`, `vta/webs/dids/list`. Every client asked only the methods it knew, so a VTA whose identities were all did:webs reported none (the wallet's persona picker, its console, `pnm did-mgmt dids list`), and each new method would add a question to every client. Design note: VTI `docs/05-design-notes/did-management.md`.

## What

- **`vta/dids/_shared/0.2`** — CONVENTIONS §20 (*Every identity: list, get and methods*): which identities are summarised (every one the VTA holds a record of, any level, including the did:key identities it minted; not did:peer, which it keeps no record of), who sees what (context access per identity; unreachable answers as absent), the `DidSummary` record, and `methods/list`. §3.1's level-1 refusal is scoped to the key-role tasks. §18 adds a tenth profile heading, *Summary details*, defining each method's `methodDetails` member, so a method is added by a profile, never by a schema change. New `key.md` profile (ineligible for key roles; exists for §20). `did-summary.schema.json`: `DidSummary`, `MethodInfo`, `DidClass`.
- **`vta/dids/list/0.1`**, **`get/0.1`**, **`methods/list/0.1`**.
- **`vta/contexts/update-did/1.2`** — the DID must be one the VTA holds in that context (`notHeld`), of a class that may be its identity (`didClassConflict`, VTI-KEY-193). 1.1 stored any syntactically valid DID.
- **`vta/contexts/delete/1.2`** — every DID in the subtree is deleted as its own method's delete task deletes it, host work settled first under the same `hostCleanupFailed` / `abandonHostCopies` rules. 1.1 named did:webvh only, so a did:webs record was dropped while its key event log stayed published as a live identity — the outcome 1.1 itself forbids for did:webvh ("removing only the consumer's own record of a DID is not a deletion of it").
- **`vta/contexts/preview-delete/2.0`** — `dids` (every method) replaces `webvhDids`, which left did:webs out of the confirmation an operator was shown.
- **Retired** `vta/webvh/dids/list/1.0` and `vta/webs/dids/list/0.1` → `vta/dids/list/0.1`.

Bindings regenerated for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart. `npm run build`, `npm run check` and `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --all-targets` pass locally.

Implementations: VTI (VTA, vta-sdk, pnm) and pnm-browser-plugin, cut over together.

title: fix(console)!: speak acl 0.3 — every grant states what its subject may use reads for
body:
The VTA serves `acl/{grant,show,update,change-role,revoke}` 0.3 and `acl/list` 0.4 only (AclEntry 0.3), so the console's access pane was refused on every write and read against a current agent. Found while refreshing `task-surface.json`, whose census flagged all five 0.2 URIs as no longer in vta-sdk.

AclEntry 0.3 makes `purposes` **REQUIRED** (VTI-ACL-100 – 110): what the subject may use content it reads for — `{scope: "any"}` (any purpose except model training) or a listed set.

- **The grant form asks, with no default.** Choosing `any` on the operator's behalf would widen every grant nobody thought about. *Only these purposes* with nothing listed is not an answer either: an empty list is malformed, not `any`. *Grant access* stays disabled until there is one.
- **The access table shows each entry's purposes**, and draws an absent one as *not stated*, never as `any` — the spec is explicit that reading absence as `any` reads a narrowed entry as wider than it is.
- Updates send only the members that change, so an existing entry's purposes are untouched by them.

Pins moved; generated modules regenerated; `task-surface.json` resynced from vta-sdk 0.90.0. Tests: `no grant is sent until its purposes are answered`, `purposesFrom reads no answer as none, never as any`, and the existing grant tests now pin `purposes` on the entry. `npm test` and `npm run build` pass.

Writing an entry: you don't. Write a conventional-commit PR title and a real commit body — see CONTRIBUTING.md and https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/blob/main/RELEASING.md.

Unreleased

Repository — the changelog convention is signposted, enforced, and current (#935)

No crate versions change. Recorded here because it changes where contributors are told to write changelog entries and what CI does about it — exactly the kind of process change changelog.d/README.md asks for a fragment about.

CHANGELOG.md opened with a ## Unreleased section that stopped at #876, while every entry since — 52 fragments — lived in changelog.d/ with nothing in the file saying so.

Signposting. CHANGELOG.md gains a note above ## Unreleased: unreleased entries live in changelog.d/ until a release is cut, this file lags that directory by design, and reading both is how you see everything pending. Above the heading deliberately — collate-changelog.sh inserts fragments immediately after the ## Unreleased line, so a note underneath would sink below the newest entries on every release. CONTRIBUTING.md's PR checklist asked for "CHANGELOG.md updated for user-facing changes" — the one thing the convention forbids, told to every contributor at the moment they were about to do it; it now asks for a fragment, beside a new Changelog section. README.md names both locations.

Enforcement. scripts/check-changelogs.sh gains two rules, because the convention had been documented in four places and enforced in none — and the cost of ignoring it never lands on the author, it lands on every other open PR as a conflict they did not cause:

  • A fragment a PR adds must name that PR, in its filename and in its ### heading. The heading half is the easy mistake — you write the fragment before the PR exists, guess the next number, and lose the race — and it is the worse one, because a wrong number survives collation and permanently points readers at an unrelated PR. Only files this PR adds are checked; the directory holds every open PR's fragment.

vta-sdk 0.21.0 / vta-keys 0.2.0 / vta-service 0.14.0 — the workspace moves to curve25519-dalek 5 (#887)

ed25519-dalek 2 → 3, x25519-dalek 2 → 3, curve25519-dalek 4 → 5 and hpke 0.13 → 0.14. These shipped together on 2026-07-06 (hpke on 07-09) and bring the next-generation RustCrypto stack with them: rand_core 0.10, signature 3, ed25519 3, aead 0.6.

vta-sdk was the single reason curve25519-dalek 4 could not leave the affinidi-tdk-rs graph. It pinned curve25519-dalek = "4" directly, plus ed25519-dalek 2, x25519-dalek 2 and hpke 0.13, and every TDK consumer inherits that through the mediator.

  • vta-sdk: breaking. Dalek types sit in public signatures — protocols::acl_management::swap::build_swap_presentation takes &ed25519_dalek::SigningKey — so callers must move to ed25519-dalek 3 in step. sealed_transfer::hpke loses its hand-rolled OsCsprng adapter, which existed only to bridge getrandom onto hpke 0.13's rand_core 0.9 traits; hpke 0.14 ships OS-CSPRNG variants of single_shot_seal / gen_keypair backed by UnwrapErr(SysRng), the same panic-on-CSPRNG-failure posture the adapter documented. The sealed-transfer wire format is unchanged and the randomness posture is unchanged.
  • vta-keys: ephemeral X25519 wrapping-key generation moves to rand::rng(). rand 0.10 renamed OsRng → SysRng and made it fallible (TryRng<Error = SysError>), so it no longer satisfies dalek's CryptoRng bound; rand_core 0.10 has no OsRng at all.
  • vta-service: two sites passed an ed25519-dalek-bip32 SigningKey straight into a workspace slot. That crate (0.3, last released 2023-08) still pins ed25519-dalek 2 and has no v3, so its SigningKey is now a different type — they cross the boundary as raw bytes, which is what every other derivation site here already did.

ed25519-dalek-bip32 keeps a dalek-2 subtree in vta-service, vta-keys and didcomm-test. It is contained: the crate is absent from vta-sdk's dependency tree, so it never reaches TDK consumers. title: feat(vta-signing): a small signing library the VTA and its callers share
body:
Title
feat(vta-signing): a small signing library the VTA and its callers share

Body
## What and why

A service that signs with its own keys, when still need have a local signing option and to avoid have its own signing implementation (the Affinidi agent gateway) had to link
the whole `vta-service` library to get the VTA's signing code. That dragged in
the storage, ACL and audit code, about 290 extra packages, three licences
`cargo deny` refuses, and a Docker build that runs out of memory. This change
moves the signing code into a small crate, `vta-signing`, that the VTA and any
such service both use.

**New crate `vta-signing` (0.1.0).** It has no workspace dependencies. It holds
only the byte-building and signing: Ed25519 and P-256 signing behind a `Signer`
trait, the JWS and SSHSIG framing, `eddsa-jcs-2022` Data Integrity proofs, and
verification. It holds no keys, no storage, no network access and no
`unsafe` (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`). Its dependency closure is about 85
crates. Key storage, a KMS or an HSM would plug in behind `Signer`.

**The VTA behaves the same.** `vta-service`, `vta-sdk` and `vta-keys` now build
and make their signatures with `vta-signing` instead of their own copies.
Storage, custody, ACL, audit and quotas are untouched. Outputs are
byte-identical, pinned by characterization tests that pass on the old and the
new code.

- `vta-signing`: `canonical`, `di`, `did_methods`, `error`, `framing`, `jws`,
  `key`, `refusal`, `sshsig`. Includes the `x5c` closure and the forbidden
  header members of the JWS rules.
- `vta-sdk`: re-exports the signing framing, the SSHSIG statement and the
  forbidden header members from `vta-signing`, so existing paths keep working.
  The non-exhaustive census is updated for the moved paths.
- `vta-service`: `sign_formats.rs` is a thin facade over the crate. The signing
  steps of `keys.rs` (imported, derived, derive-and-sign), `sign_jws` and
  `sign_document` use the crate's two-phase API.
- `vta-keys`: `internal::sign` uses the crate, with equivalence tests against
  `affinidi_crypto` and `ed25519-dalek`.
- `Dockerfile.nitro` copies the new crate. `CLAUDE.md`, `vta-service/CLAUDE.md`,
  the workspace engineering notes and the decomposition note are updated.

**Not moved.** CSR building stays in the VTA. The roughly thirty other raw
signing sites (Trust Task proofs, holder proofs, rooms, voting, did:webvh
updates, `derive_and_sign_document`) are untouched. The crate's README lists
what is not here yet.

Also in this PR: the offline CLI's break-glass writes are audited. This is
the one behaviour change. The offline vta CLI has no authenticated caller and
makes no authorization decision, so a write it made to who holds authority
left no trace in the audit log. vta acl create, vta acl update, vta acl delete
and the context create command (including the admin ACL entry it can create)
now record an audit row with actor "vta-cli (break-glass)", channel "vta-cli",
the resource and, where there is one, the context. The row is written before
the store is persisted, and a failure to write it fails the command, so such a
change can't happen without leaving a record. Nothing else about the CLI
changes.

**Tests.**
- 52 tests in `vta-signing`.
- 6 characterization tests, `sign_characterization_tests.rs`, that fix what
  the signing operations produce for a fixed key (The same file, copied
unchanged onto main, passes there too).
- Offline CLI audit integration tests, offline_cli_audit.rs.
- Full workspace: `cargo nextest` 7167/7167, plus `vtc-service` and
  `vtc-client` 3645/3645.
- Doc tests pass; `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets
  -- -D warnings` are clean; `vta-enclave` builds.

## Requirements

VTI-KEY-163 (the proof's method and issuer in one form): a comment that
referenced it moves with the code, and the rule is unchanged.

## Backport

none

## Checklist

- [x] Targets `main` (or is a backport / `release-direct` PR into `release/<name>`)
- [x] No `version =` edits in any `Cargo.toml` (the new crate's own manifest has
      its first version, `0.1.0`; nothing existing is bumped)
- [x] Tests cover the change; `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean
