title: build(deps)!: affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.47, TDK 0.45, trust-tasks 0.39 and mediator 0.52, with delivery receipts and mediator wake
body:
Step 2 of the coordinated release: VTI onto `affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.47.2 / `affinidi-tdk` 0.45 / `trust-tasks-*` 0.39 / mediator 0.52 (affinidi/affinidi-messaging-mediator#283), and the receipts and mediator-wake work those releases carry. Breaking (`!`): the dependency moves change types in published crates' public APIs (`affinidi-crypto` 0.3 `KeyType`, `trust-tasks-rs` 0.39, `affinidi-sd-jwt` 0.2, `affinidi-vc` 0.3, `affinidi-mdoc` 0.6), `vti_common::trust_task_push::TspPushTransport` is now built with `TspPushTransport::new` (it carries private state), and `vta_sdk::schema_cache` is now a wrapper over `trust_tasks_rs::validate` (`CompiledSchema` is gone; `SchemaError` is `trust_tasks_rs::validate::ValidationError`). ## 1. Dependencies - `affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.47.2, `-core` 0.1.12, `-delivery` 0.2.0, `-didcomm` 0.15.14; `affinidi-tdk` 0.45 with what it drags: `affinidi-crypto` 0.3, `affinidi-data-integrity` 0.8.7, `affinidi-did-common` 0.4.7, `affinidi-vc` 0.3, `affinidi-sd-jwt` 0.2 / `-sd-jwt-vc` 0.3, `affinidi-mdoc` 0.6, `affinidi-oid4vc-core` 0.1.11, `affinidi-openid4vp` 0.1.5, `affinidi-secrets-resolver` 0.5.18, `affinidi-did-webs` 0.13.4, `affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk` 0.8.53. - `trust-tasks-rs`, `-proof`, `-https`, `-didcomm`, `-tsp`, `-capability-client` 0.39 — the one copy the SDK uses, so a single `trust-tasks-rs` across the boundary. - `affinidi-messaging-test-mediator`, `-mediator-admin`, `-mediator-tui` 0.52. - Adapted: - `affinidi-sd-jwt` 0.2 builds the kb-jwt verifier from the credential's own `cnf.jwk` and requires `aud`, `nonce` and a fresh `iat`. The VTC's OID4VP verifier (`credentials::exchange::verify`) now passes a `KeyBindingCheck` with a 600 s `iat` window (`KB_JWT_MAX_AGE_SECS`, RFC 9901 §7.3) — before, the kb-jwt `iat` was not checked at all. Receive-time verification (no key binding) is unchanged. - `affinidi-crypto` 0.3 key pairs implement `Drop` (zeroize); test fixtures clone the bytes they used to move. - `cargo deny`: passes with `multiple-versions = "deny"`. `fancy-regex` skip removed; `jsonschema-value:<0.60` added (new in jsonschema 0.49's graph). The `jsonschema:<0.60` and `jsonwebtoken:<11` skips stay: `trust-tasks-rs` 0.39 is on jsonschema 0.49 and `trust-tasks-https` 0.39 on jsonwebtoken 10, both upstream. ## 2. #2622 / #2655 — schema compilation and the duplicate jsonschema - `jsonschema-trust-tasks` (jsonschema 0.46 under another name) is gone from the workspace. `vta_sdk::schema_cache` is now a thin wrapper over `trust_tasks_rs::validate::SchemaValidator`: one process-wide `SCHEMAS` instance for `check(schema, value)`, and `check_payload::

` is `ValidatedPayload::validate_value`, which `trust-tasks-rs` 0.39 caches itself. Every call site #2622 names (`validate_payload`, `check_payload_conforms`, `room_act`, `notifications`, `client::rooms`, `protocols::vetting`) already went through `schema_cache` and now compiles each schema once through `trust-tasks-rs`. `protocols::vetting::against_definition` keeps its per-definition text (built once, leaked; the set is fixed by call sites) and validates it through the same cache. - Remaining per-call compile, not in #2622's list: `vtc-service/src/rooms/storage_credentials.rs::check_cleartext` (a schema built from a `$defs` entry per call). Left for a follow-up. - #2655: the jsonschema duplicate drops from 0.46/0.60 to 0.49/0.60 but does not go away (upstream `trust-tasks-rs`), nor does jsonwebtoken 10/11 (`trust-tasks-https`), nor the RustCrypto/rand/tungstenite/tower-http/base64 lines the issue lists. So `Refs`, not `Closes`. ## 3. #2553 — delivery receipts (VTI-TRN-042 as amended, VTI-TRN-060 – 064) - Every messaging service is built `MessagingService::with_receipts` with an `AtmReceiptPacker` for its own profile: the VTA's main session, the collector's persona sessions, the watch-address sessions and the transient handshake; the VTC's session; and `vta-sdk`'s `DIDCommSession` (so every Rust client receipts what asks). A message that asks is receipted to its authenticated sender once handed off (VTI-TRN-061). - The confirmation sweep runs with the service's `receipt_reach()` (`vti_common::outbox_store::confirmation_loop`, which wraps `confirmation_loop_with_reach` with the delivery layer's settle-unconfirmed default, which it does not export). - Push engine (`vti_common::trust_task_push`): - DIDComm attempts ask for a receipt under the attempt's outbox key (`request_receipt`, the `delivery_id` header); TSP attempts carry it as the envelope's `deliveryId` (`affinidi_messaging_sdk::delivery::tsp_envelope`, replacing `vta_sdk::tsp_binding::wrap_envelope` there). - Cross-mediator (nested) TSP sends are scoped `DeliveryScope::Relayed`, same-mediator ones `Local`. `SendReceipt` has no scope field, so `TspPushTransport` answers `MessageTransport::delivery_scope` from the route it chose on the send the drain just made (the drain asks right after). Divergence from the brief's "`with_scope(Relayed)`": the entry is written by `MessagingService::send_via`, not by the engine, so the transport is the one place the scope can be stated. - The sweep finishes a `Sent`/`Unconfirmed` attempt that was relayed to a recipient not in `ReceiptReach` (or that the delivery layer settled `NoEvidencePath`) with evidence `unconfirmable`, logged at `info`, and does **not** escalate. A recipient known to receipt escalates as before; `Local` attempts are confirmed by the status poll as before. - `VtiOutboxStore` logs a `NoEvidencePath` settle at `info`, not `warn`. - `vtc/join-requests/status`: the pinned `0.1` response has no `credentialsDelivery` member (`additionalProperties: false`; only `credentialsDelivered: bool`), so none was added. ## 4. #2663 — waking a device through its own mediator (design C; VTI-TRN-070 – 074, VTI-APV-024) - Pinned in `vti-specs-core` with the trust-tasks CLI: `messaging/wake/set/0.1`, `messaging/wake/request/0.1`, `messaging/receipt/0.1`. - `step_up::trigger_gateway_wake` keeps the ACL `DeviceBinding` wake channel first. With none, `messaging::mediator_wake::request_wake` waits (≤ 60 s) for the push's first attempt to be handed off, reads the id the recipient's mediator stores it under (`trust_task_push::stored_message_id`, the attempt's hop id), and sends one `trust_tasks().wake_request(profile, approver_mediator, addressee, &[id], Interactive)`. An id named once is never named again (VTI-TRN-072); once per push. - The mediator's `messaging/wake/request/0.1#response` (always `{}`) is dropped as a reply no waiter claimed (pinned by a test). An older mediator's refusal (`trust-task-error` from a mediator asked within 2 min) is consumed quietly by the inbound spine and that mediator is not asked again for an hour — the device collects on its next connection, as before. - `retry_safety`: not classified. `vta_sdk::retry_safety` covers the tasks this VTA *serves* (`ALL_URIS`, with a census that fails on an entry outside it). The VTA only sends `wake/request` (fire-and-forget, through the SDK); `receipt` is consumed by the delivery layer before dispatch; `wake/set` is a device → mediator task. `spec_pin_census` is green. ## Behaviour the new releases brought, adapted - **Half-open acceptance window** (trust-tasks-rs 0.39): a document is refused once `issuedAt + max_age + skew` is at or before `now` (it was after). `vti_common::trust_task::acceptance::AcceptanceWindow::refuses` and the push engine's `refused_when_collected` now agree with the consumer policy at the edge (VTI-TRN-044/045/047); the boundary tests in vti-common, vta-service and vtc-service move by one second. - **Mediator 0.52 refuses a forward to a DID with no account** (affinidi-messaging-mediator changelog: "a forward is delivered only to a next hop that has an account"). A room-watch address gets its account when its connection first opens, so `rooms/keys/watch` now waits (≤ 15 s, while the address supervisor runs) for a fresh address's connection before arming the host. Without it a host signal sent in the first seconds was refused and lost. The e2e "signal queued before the address connects" test now models a restart of an address that has connected before. - affinidi-data-integrity 0.8.7 carries every VC Data Integrity §2.1 proof member, so the uncarried-member test uses a non-§2.1 member; affinidi-mdoc 0.6 requires a device key in `MdocBuilder` (test fixtures). ## Tests - `vti-common` `trust_task_push::receipt_tests`: a receipt settles `Delivered` only from the addressed party (a stranger's settles nothing and teaches `ReceiptReach` nothing); relayed with no receipt → `unconfirmable`, never moved to another transport; a known receipt sender still escalates; a `Local` attempt is still confirmed by the status poll and a `Relayed` one is never asked; the stored id is the handed-off attempt's hop id; attempts ask for receipts under their outbox key over DIDComm and TSP. - `vta-service`: no ACL wake channel → the mediator is asked once; with one → it is not; a pending request is not rung again; an older mediator's refusal is quiet and remembered; the wake `#response` and the refusal are answered with nothing by the spine. ## Notes - For openvtc: `MockVta` already lives in `vta-test-support`. Refs #2655 Closes #2622 Closes #2553 Closes #2663

body:
build(deps)!: affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.47, TDK 0.45, trust-tasks 0.39 and mediator 0.52, with delivery receipts and mediator wake (#2741)

* build(deps)!: move to affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.47, affinidi-tdk 0.45 and trust-tasks 0.39

affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.47.2 (-core 0.1.12, -delivery 0.2.0), affinidi-tdk
0.45 with what it carries (affinidi-crypto 0.3, data-integrity 0.8.7,
did-common 0.4.7, vc 0.3, sd-jwt 0.2, sd-jwt-vc 0.3, mdoc 0.6,
oid4vc-core 0.1.11), trust-tasks-* 0.39 (the SDK's own copy, so one
trust-tasks-rs across the boundary) and mediator 0.52 (test-mediator,
-admin, -tui).

affinidi-sd-jwt 0.2 builds the kb-jwt verifier from the credential's own
cnf.jwk and requires aud, nonce and a fresh iat: the VTC's OpenID4VP
verifier now checks the kb-jwt iat (600 s, RFC 9901 §7.3), which it did
not before.

SchemaValidator, so the private jsonschema 0.46 copy
(jsonschema-trust-tasks) is gone. CompiledSchema is removed and
SchemaError is trust_tasks_rs::validate::ValidationError.

cargo deny: the fancy-regex skip goes; jsonschema and jsonwebtoken stay
duplicated upstream (trust-tasks-rs 0.39 on jsonschema 0.49,
trust-tasks-https 0.39 on jsonwebtoken 10).

Refs #2655
Closes #2622

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(messaging)!: delivery receipts and an unconfirmable outcome for relayed pushes

Every messaging service is built MessagingService::with_receipts with an
AtmReceiptPacker for its own profile (the VTA's session, collector, watch
addresses and transient handshake; the VTC's; vta-sdk's DIDCommSession),
so a message that asks for a receipt is receipted to its authenticated
sender (VTI-TRN-061). The confirmation sweep runs with the service's
receipt reach.

The push engine asks for a receipt on every DIDComm and TSP attempt under
the attempt's outbox key (VTI-TRN-060), scopes cross-mediator TSP sends
Relayed, and finishes a relayed attempt to a recipient not known to send
receipts as `unconfirmable` instead of escalating it (VTI-TRN-042 as
amended, VTI-TRN-064). A recipient known to receipt escalates as before;
same-mediator attempts are confirmed by the status poll as before. A
NoEvidencePath settle logs at info, not warn.

TspPushTransport is now built with TspPushTransport::new.

Closes #2553

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta-service): wake a device through its own mediator when it has no ACL wake channel

Design C of #2663 (VTI-TRN-070 – 074, VTI-APV-024). trigger_gateway_wake
keeps the ACL DeviceBinding wake channel first. With none, the VTA waits
for the push's first attempt to be handed off and sends one
messaging/wake/request/0.1 to the recipient's mediator, naming the
message by the id that mediator stores it under. An id named once is
never named again (VTI-TRN-072). The mediator's constant #response is
dropped as a reply no waiter claimed; an older mediator's refusal is
consumed quietly and that mediator is not asked again for an hour, so
the device collects on its next connection as before.

Pins messaging/wake/set/0.1, messaging/wake/request/0.1 and
messaging/receipt/0.1 in vti-specs-core.

Closes #2663

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service): adapt to trust-tasks 0.39, mdoc 0.6 and mediator 0.52 behaviour

- trust-tasks-rs 0.39 applies the acceptance window half-open: a document
  is refused once issuedAt + max_age + skew is at or before now.
  AcceptanceWindow::refuses and the push engine's refused_when_collected
  now agree with it (VTI-TRN-044/045/047), and the boundary tests move.
- affinidi-data-integrity 0.8.7 carries every VC Data Integrity §2.1
  proof member (challenge, domain, expires, id, previousProof), so the
  "uncarried member" test uses a member outside §2.1.
- affinidi-mdoc 0.6 requires a device key on MdocBuilder; test fixtures
  supply one.
- affinidi-sd-jwt 0.2 checks the kb-jwt iat: the expired-credential test
  uses a fresh kb-jwt, and a stale kb-jwt has its own test.
- Mediator 0.52 refuses a forward to a DID with no account there, and a
  watch address gets its account when its connection first opens. An
  arming now waits (up to 15 s, while the address supervisor runs) for a
  fresh address's connection before arming the host, so a signal sent
  before it opens is not refused and lost.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* build(deps): resolve Cargo.lock against the published mediator 0.52.0

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-vault): verify bbs-2023 derived proofs with the presentation header bound

affinidi-data-integrity 0.8.7 deprecates verify_derived_proof and
verify_pseudonym_derived_proof, which cannot check the presentation
header. The VTC's OpenID4VP verifier now has the library refuse a derived
proof made for another challenge too (it already compared the header
itself), and the vault's base-proof check binds its own nonce.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

title: vtc-service-v0.30.0
body:
### Added - **rooms**: Load older by version (records/list 0.8, keys/browse 0.6) and host limits in rooms/info 0.5 ([#2727](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2727)) * build(vti-specs-rooms): pin rooms/records/list 0.8, rooms/keys/browse 0.6, rooms/info 0.5 trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1289, for #2294 points 3 and 4. Older versions stay pinned beside them while they are still served or sent. The registry's in-place refresh of rooms/records/put 0.1-0.5 and rooms/keys/list 0.2 (marking them superseded) is left out: adopting put/0.6 is separate work. ### Build & CI - Harden CI and the build: pinned toolchain, image digests, release-token checks, advisories, fuzzing, tooling lint ([#2709](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2709)) * build: pin the Rust toolchain to 1.95.0 and pass clippy 1.95 ([#2658](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2658)) rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.95.0, the workspace rust-version and the Dockerfiles' Rust image. CI jobs install it with scripts/install-rust-toolchain.sh instead of a floating stable, so a new Rust release's lints can no longer turn main red with no code change; Dependabot proposes the next one as a PR. scripts/check-toolchain-pins.sh keeps the pin at or above the MSRV and the Dockerfiles in line. Clippy 1.95 is stricter than the stable CI ran in nonminimal_bool and collapsible_match: De Morgan rewrites at eleven call sites (behaviour unchanged), Option::take().map in vta-persona, and one allow on vti_voting::audit::check_order, where a match guard would fall through to later arms. - **deps**: Enforce cargo-deny bans/sources, drop unused deps, hoist shared deps, forbid unsafe ([#2708](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2708)) * build(deps): enforce cargo-deny bans/sources, drop unused deps, hoist shared deps, forbid unsafe pgp, openssl only via webauthn-rs 0.5, no wildcards, and multiple-versions = "deny" with a skip list of today's duplicates grouped by cause. The two advisory ignores cargo-deny reports as not detected (RUSTSEC-2026-0381, RUSTSEC-2024-0436) are removed, the stale [graph] comment rewritten, and the yanked crypto-bigint 0.7.6 moved to 0.7.11. ring leaves the VTA and VTC graphs; it stays only under attest-verify. removed from 19 crates; deliberate ones are listed under [package.metadata.cargo-machete] ignored. A tier-0 "manifest hygiene" CI job runs cargo-machete and the lint check. once in [workspace.dependencies]; vta-tee inherits aws-lc-rs. The five crypto crates carry real minimum-patch floors, enforced by check-workspace-version-reqs.py. (check-workspace-lints.py); unsafe_code = "forbid" workspace-wide, with the four crates that need unsafe restating the table at "deny" and rewritten safely. The two missing publish = false comments are added. ### Changed - **vtc**: One typed routing table for every Trust Task family; routes/ is the HTTP surface only ([#2732](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2732)) * refactor(vtc): route every Trust Task family through one typed AsyncDispatcher #2728 split trust_tasks/mod.rs into handler files but left three routing styles: about sixty direct arms in `dispatch_typed`, thirty-three family modules each keeping a `URIS` list beside a `match` that re-matched it (one `FAMILIES` table arm), and typed `AsyncDispatcher` registration for rooms and git-ns. A hand-kept `DISPATCHED_URIS` (540 lines) had to agree with all of it, and already did not: `auth/step-up/requests/show/0.1` was routed but not listed, so discovery never advertised it. - `trust_tasks::routing`: one `AsyncDispatcher` every family registers on, keyed on the generated payload type (`on!(routes, P => handler)`). The URI a handler answers is `P::TYPE_URI`; the served set is the table itself (`routing::served_uris`), and `dispatched_uris()` (that plus discovery) replaces `DISPATCHED_URIS` for the unsupported-version hint, discovery, the size gate and the censuses. - Each family exposes `register(Routes) -> Routes`; every `URIS` constant, every family `dispatch` and the `FAMILIES` table are gone, and the direct arms moved into their handler files' `register`. Families whose verbs share an authority check before the payload is read (backup, website, the administrator's passkeys) route through a small `Op` enum, not a URI match. - Handlers are registered on `Received

`: routed and policed as `P`, but handed the JSON as received, so every handler still reads it against the schema before parsing it and still resolves the signer's authority before reading the payload (a typed downcast in the router would reverse that order and change which refusal a stranger gets). - Censuses: no URI is registered twice (the dispatcher would silently keep the later one), and none is also a rooms or git-ns task. - The URI constants nothing but the removed lists named are deleted; the ones only tests name stay behind `#[cfg(test)]`. Behaviour is unchanged except that discovery and the version hint now list `auth/step-up/requests/show/0.1`, which was always served. - **vta**: Decouple vta-cli-common, split key/room modules, extract vta-test-support, share reject helpers and service plumbing ([#2730](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2730)) * refactor(vta): put vta-cli-common and dialoguer behind cli-synthesis ([#2566](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2566)) Only the `vta` binary's offline CLI modules and setup wizard use them, and the binary already requires `cli-synthesis`. The library — and so vta-enclave — no longer compiles vtc-client, ratatui, qrcode, dialoguer or crossterm: `cargo tree -p vta-enclave -e normal` drops from 981 to ~935 unique lines. The vti-rooms comment claimed `default-features = false` kept the host half out of the build; feature unification through vti-rooms-dtg (which verifies through `vti_rooms::authz`) turns `host` back on. Say so, and why it costs nothing new. - **rooms**: Share the rooms/* handlers between hosts and run every host receive path on Spine ([#2731](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2731)) * refactor(room-host): receive every document through vti_trust_task_server::Spine room-host re-implemented the receive pipeline inline: size, freshness, validate_basic and the accepted-id claim/settle, with no spec-policy step and the proof verified lazily inside each handler. It now runs the shared Spine the VTC runs ([#2576](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2576)): the size gate holds each task to its declared maxDocumentBytes, the spec policy comes from vti_specs::schema_index::spec_policy_for, the proof is verified once over the document as received and bound to its issuer, DIDComm and TSP frames carry their authenticated sender so the spine binds it (VTI-OPS-021/093), and the duplicate-id record is StoreAcceptedIds (VTI-OPS-025..029). A host without a DID still refuses an expired document: the spine skips the recipient binding then, so before_proof applies the expiry check. A proof made by someone other than the issuer is now proofInvalid, as at the VTC, rather than permissionDenied. - **vtc**: Vtc-audit leaf crate, one regorus engine, typed error codes, trust_tasks split, AdminActor ([#2728](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2728)) * refactor(vti-common)!: move the VTC's audit-event vocabulary to a new vtc-audit leaf crate ### Documentation - **vtc-service**: Decomposition plan and where it stops ([#2725](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2725)) Measured on 6cf8ad034: 364k lines, AppState with 87 fields (52 keyspace handles). Step order: compile-time baseline, vtc-keyspaces leaf, per-subsystem store structs inside the crate, then policy (after #2577) and the acl core (after #2580), the registry pure half, and rooms via #2575's shared crate. Orders #2568, #2579, #2574 against it. Under 10% of src/ is extractable; the spine stays. - Operator guides, CLI remediation strings and the crate map match the tree, checked in CI ([#2706](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2706)) * fix(cli): operator-facing remediation strings name commands that parse Every error, hint and --help string that tells an operator what to run now names a command the current pnm / vta / cnm accepts ([#2631](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2631)): the retired `pnm webvh …` / `vta webvh …` surface becomes `did-mgmt servers|dids …`, `pnm auth login` (pnm has none) becomes `pnm setup`, `pnm acl delete` takes the DID positionally, `list-domains` sits under `dids`, the backup descriptor hints no longer name `pnm backup save|restore`, and stale doc comments (`pnm passkey-enroll-token`, `vta export-mnemonic`, `cnm community info`) are corrected. A pnm and a vta test parse each remediation command through Cli::try_parse_from. The --template help is derived from vta_sdk::did_templates::BUILTIN_NAMES and no longer lists the retired did-hosting-* template names ([#2635](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2635)). The `rooms keys key-package` help gives the 14-day KeyPackage lifetime the code holds ([#2632](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2632)), and `rooms prune` no longer says a prune reaches the host only: members' VTAs discard rungs at or below the epoch floor ([#2633](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2633)). ### Fixed - **cli**: CLI and MCP operator UX sweep (confirmations, secrets off argv, JSON everywhere, room defaults, tool-level MCP errors) ([#2726](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2726)) * fix(cli): a corrupt profile is fatal, saves are atomic, one start-up for pnm and cnm, --version and completions - **vtc-admin-ui**: Console and member portal UX sweep (error boundaries, confirmations, modals, a11y, session expiry, dates, toasts) ([#2707](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2707)) * fix(vtc-admin-ui): an error boundary per screen, per portal page and at both roots ([#2605](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2605)) ### Performance - **rooms**: Indexed record reads, per-room locks, commits outside the host lock, per-election ballot boxes ([#2712](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2712)) * perf(vti-common): per-bundle chunk lock and a progress bitmap apart from the plan A chunked transfer's lock is striped by bundle id, so one bundle's finalize (a whole-file hash) no longer stalls every other transfer ([#2596](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2596)). Progress is a bitmap row beside the immutable plan, read from a per-process cache, so a chunk no longer re-reads and rewrites a plan of up to 4,096 digests ([#2597](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2597)). A bundle opened before the bitmap row existed keeps the progress its plan recorded; get_plan still returns the plan with its progress. - **vtc-service**: Index and seek the VTC's hot full-keyspace scans (ACL authority, VRC digest, audit, members, rooms fingerprints, directory) ([#2711](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2711)) * perf(vtc-service): an ACL authority index for approver and administrator reads ([#2602](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2602)) ### Security - **vtc-service**: Setup writes the admin key to an owner-only file, never stdout ([#2724](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2724)) The interactive `vtc setup` wizard offered to print the long-term admin DID's private key (the DidKeyMaterialV2 JSON the VTA seals to the setup key) to the terminal, where it lands in scrollback and any session recording; `setup --from` dropped it altogether and told the operator to "re-run interactively", which re-provisions. Both front-ends now share one hand-over in `apply`: the key is written to `/keys/admin-key.json` with `vti_common::secure_file:: write_secret_file` (created new, 0600, directory 0700) before the install token is minted, and only the path is printed (`admin_key_file=` in the terse block). This is the pattern setup already uses for key material that must outlive the run (`--setup-key-out`, `vtc keys request`). An existing admin-key.json is never overwritten; a re-run writes a timestamped file beside it. Docs updated to match. - Invite grants, CSRF/HSTS/cookies, x5c path checks, guarded status-list fetch, vault zeroize, consent payload types ([#2710](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2710)) * security(vtc): a wallet admin invitation's entry expires with it until claimed, and goes with a revoke ([#2660](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2660)) vtc/admin/invites/create/0.2 item 3 writes a wallet invitation's administrator entry when the invitation is issued, and the code wrote it permanent: revoking the invitation (which create 0.2 says withdraws the authority it confers) or letting it lapse left an unexpiring community administrator nobody claimed. The entry is now written to expire with the invitation and recorded beside it (install::InviteGrant, keyed by jti). vtc/install/claim/finish/0.3 makes it permanent once the DID has proved itself with the token and claim code; vtc/admin/invites/revoke/0.1, and the void after five wrong claim codes, remove it (with its sessions and delegations) if it is still exactly what the invitation wrote. A lapsed or still-provisional entry no longer blocks a new invitation for the same DID. The offline `vtc admin invite --did` writes the same provisional entry. Deferring the write to the claim, as passkey invitations do, would contradict create 0.2 item 3 and claim/finish 0.3 item 7, so the entry is still written at mint.

title: security(config): salted unlock key, AAD, encrypted activity log, atomic writes
body:
One storage-format change, with one migration path, for #566, #569, #568, #567, #564 and #570. Every issue was checked against current `main`; the line numbers in them were out of date, the findings were not.

Built on #597 (unlock prompt, `UnlockCode::for_existing`, wizard/import key derivation off the render task, Settings passphrase forms). #597 and #599 merged while this was in progress, so the branch is rebased onto `main` and is no longer stacked; it keeps all of #597's behaviour, including short pre-0.8 unlock codes still opening their profile.

## Per issue

**#566 — per-profile random Argon2 salt.**
- New secured-config envelope `{"format":"PasswordSealed","salt":…,"sealed":…}`. The key is Argon2id (same parameters) over the unlock code with 16 random bytes of salt drawn when the code is *set* (setup wizard, headless setup, backup import, Settings → Change Protection). The salt is stored beside the ciphertext.
- `UnlockCode` now holds the code (`SecretString`), not a key. `check_unlock_code` / `load` read the blob, derive with the blob's salt (or the legacy fixed salt for an old blob), and cache the derived key on the `UnlockCode`, so the prompt's check and the load after it run Argon2 once. `load_fast` warms the salted key synchronously before the async load, so no Argon2 runs on the runtime.
- `Config::unlock_code` is a new `UnlockKey` (salt + zeroizing key, redacted `Debug`); every save seals with it directly — no Argon2 per save.
- Legacy `PasswordEncrypted` blobs (tagged or the older untagged shape) open with the legacy KDF and are rewritten as `PasswordSealed` during that same successful load (see migration below).

**#569 — AAD and domain separation.**
- Secured blob: HKDF info `openvtc/secured-config/v2`, AAD `openvtc/secured-config/v2\0profile\0{profile}` (the keyring account name).
- Protected blob in `config.json`: `"OPC2" | nonce | ct+tag`, HKDF info `openvtc/protected-config/v2`, AAD `openvtc/protected-config/v2\0profile\0{profile}`. Legacy (unprefixed, `openvtc-key-v2`, no AAD) blobs still open under every key in the existing D12 fallback chain and are rewritten by the next save. A legacy blob whose random nonce happens to start with `OPC2` still opens (the legacy path is always tried after a failed `OPC2` open).
- Exports: `passphrase_encrypt_v2` (which ignored `info`) is replaced by `passphrase_encrypt`, writing `OPV3`: random salt, `info` fed into HKDF as `openvtc/passphrase-blob/v3\0{info}`, header (`OPV3 | salt`) bound as AAD. `passphrase_decrypt` reads OPV3, OPV2 and v1.
- The protected tier inside an export is now re-encrypted from the *live* config (it used to be the blob read at start-up) and bound to `export`, not to a profile, so a backup imports into any profile. `ExportedConfig::open_private` handles old and new exports.
- **Profile-name binding is a deliberate behaviour change:** renaming a profile by hand (moving its keyring entry / `config-{profile}.json`) makes it unopenable under the new name. There is no rename feature in OpenVTC; the supported way to move a profile is export + import, which is unaffected. I think that is acceptable for what it buys (a blob copied between profiles no longer opens); flagging it for review.
- Token (`TokenEncrypted`) profiles: format unchanged. Binding AAD there needs a new token envelope and touches the card path; not done here.
- Not done: the optional monotonic save counter against rollback of `config.json` (see risks).

**#568 — activity log moved to the encrypted tier.**
- `ProtectedConfig.logs` (serde default). `PublicConfig.logs` is now `legacy_logs`: read (`rename = "logs"`), never written (`skip_serializing`). `load_step2` and backup import move an old config's plaintext log into the protected tier (`Logs::absorb`: merged by time, sanitised, capped to the limit). The next save writes both tiers in the one atomic file write, so the move is crash-safe: until that save, the file is unchanged and the move simply repeats on the next load.
- `Logs::insert` sanitises every message with `openvtc_core::display::sanitize_display` (ANSI escapes, control, bidi and zero-width characters stripped) and caps it at 1024 characters, so no caller can forget.
- All 42 `config.public.logs` call sites now write `config.private.logs`.
- No `config_version` bump: the version check only rejects *older* versions, a bump would have made every existing v2 config look like a pre-v2 one (breaking reset), and older builds would not have been stopped by it anyway. The change is additive: an older build keeps the protected `logs` key in `ProtectedConfig::extra`.
- `SECURITY.md`, `README.md` and `docs/openvtc-config-data-structure.md` updated for what is in the public tier.

**#567 — atomic, owner-only writes.**
- New `openvtc_core::private_file::atomic_write_private(path, bytes)`: temp file created with `create_new` (never opens an existing file or link) in the same directory, `0600` from creation on Unix, write + `fsync`, rename, directory `fsync`; the temp file is removed on any failure before the rename. A symlink at the target is refused. `create_private_dir` creates a missing profile directory `0700` (an existing one is left alone — it may be an `OPENVTC_CONFIG_PATH` the user shares on purpose).
- Used by `PublicConfig::save` (a symlinked `config.json` is resolved and written where it points, so a deliberately relocated profile keeps working), `Config::export` (symlink refused), `Diagnosis::write_report`, and the file-backed secret store (replacing its own copy of the routine). Windows builds: permission bits are `cfg(unix)`.

**#564 — skip unchanged keyring writes.**
- `SecuredConfig::save` keeps, per profile, a SHA-256 fingerprint of what it last wrote: protection mode, the envelope parameter (unlock-key salt / token id) and the plaintext — not the ciphertext, whose nonce changes every write. An identical save returns without touching the store. Changing or removing the passphrase always writes (new salt / new mode). The record is in memory only, cleared by a failed write, by every `SecuredConfig::load`, by the migration, and by `delete_profile`.
- `key_info` is now serialised in key order so equal contents give equal plaintext bytes (a `HashMap`'s iteration order is not stable). Deserialisation is unchanged.
- "Secrets first, then file" ordering in `Config::save` is preserved: a skipped write means the stored secrets are already current.

**#570 — secret hygiene.**
- `SettingsAction::{ExportConfig, ImportConfig, SetPassphrase}` and `Action::ImportConfig` carry `SecretString`.
- Main-page `passphrase_buffer` / `confirm_buffer` are a new `SecretBuffer` (zeroizing; growth copies into a fresh zeroizing buffer, `clear` wipes, hands over a `SecretString`).
- `SuppliedUnlockCode.passphrase`, the dialoguer unlock input and `cli::read_unlock_code_file` are `Zeroizing<String>` (dialoguer's own internal buffer is out of reach).
- `secured_config`: decrypted and serialised plaintext is `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>` throughout; `save` takes `Option<&UnlockKey>`; no more bare `Vec<u8>` copies of the unlock key.
- `vetting::tickets::Ticket` has a hand-written `Debug` that redacts `code` and `secret`.
- The ticket compare uses `subtle::ConstantTimeEq` (`subtle` 2.6.1 was already in the graph; added as a direct dependency).
- `VtaSetupState.access_token` is `Option<SecretString>` (it is only ever written, so the change was contained).
- Skipped as asked: `did-git-sign`'s `InstallArgs` taking a `SecretString` is an upstream change (`git_signing.rs` still has to `expose_secret().to_string()` there).

Also fixed in passing, because the import path had to change anyway: backup import now writes the secured config *before* the config file (the order `Config::save` keeps), and only gives a profile an unlock key when the backup is unlock-code protected — previously a plaintext-protected backup was sealed under a key derived from the (possibly empty) new-code field, which the next load refused as a protection mismatch.

## On-disk format

| Blob | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Secured config, unlock code | `{"format":"PasswordEncrypted","data":b64(nonce‖ct)}`; key = Argon2id(code, SHA-256("openvtc-unlock-code-v1")); HKDF info `openvtc-key-v2`; no AAD | `{"format":"PasswordSealed","salt":b64(16 random bytes),"sealed":b64(nonce‖ct)}`; key = Argon2id(code, salt); HKDF info `openvtc/secured-config/v2`; AAD `openvtc/secured-config/v2\0profile\0{profile}` |
| Secured config, token / plaintext | unchanged | unchanged |
| `config.json` `private` | `b64(nonce‖ct)`, HKDF info `openvtc-key-v2`, no AAD | `b64("OPC2"‖nonce‖ct)`, HKDF info `openvtc/protected-config/v2`, AAD `…\0profile\0{profile}` (in an export: `…\0export`) |
| `config.json` `logs` | plaintext activity log | absent; the log is inside `private` |
| Export file | `OPV2‖salt‖nonce‖ct`, `info` unused, no AAD | `OPV3‖salt‖nonce‖ct`, HKDF info `openvtc/passphrase-blob/v3\0{info}`, AAD `OPV3‖salt` |

`PasswordSealed` deliberately names its payload `sealed`, not `data`: an older build that meets an unknown variant falls back to its untagged legacy parse, and a shared `data` field would let that parse treat the blob as a legacy one and report the right code as wrong. With no field in common it reports the blob as unrecognised instead (pinned by a test).

## Migration and crash safety

The legacy secured blob is upgraded inside `SecuredConfig::load`, after it has been opened with the code the user typed:

1. Derive a key under a fresh random salt (warmed in `load_fast`, so this is a cache hit at load), seal the same plaintext as `PasswordSealed`, and open it again in memory. Nothing is written unless it round-trips.
2. One `set_secret` replacing the one entry. Every backend replaces an entry as a unit (Keychain item update, Secret Service replace, the file store's temp+rename). Before it, the legacy blob is stored; after it, the sealed one.
3. Read the entry back and open it with the new key. If that fails, write the original bytes back and report the upgrade as failed.

Both versions open with the same unlock code because `load` and `check_unlock_code` dispatch on the stored variant, so a crash before, during or after step 2 leaves a profile that opens; a failed upgrade is logged, the load still succeeds, and the next save writes the new format anyway. The protected tier is encrypted under `protected_key`, which lives *inside* the secured blob and does not change, so it needs no coordinated second write. The protected tier's own move to `OPC2` and the log move both happen in the single atomic write of `config.json`, and old forms keep opening, so there is no state between two files that fails to load. `check_unlock_code` works for both formats.

## Behaviour changes

- After the first unlock on this version, a passphrase profile cannot be opened by an earlier release (reported as an unrecognised store blob). `config.json` written by this version likewise does not open in an earlier release (its protected blob does not decrypt there). Downgrading needs an export taken *before* upgrading.
- One extra Argon2 run (~1 s), once, on the first unlock of a legacy profile.
- A profile renamed by hand no longer opens (see #569 above).
- A symlink at an export path is refused. A symlinked `config.json` is followed (written where it points), as before, but now atomically.
- The first save after start-up always writes the keyring; later identical saves do not. If something outside OpenVTC deletes the keyring entry mid-session, it is no longer silently rewritten by the next unrelated save.
- Log messages lose control/bidi/zero-width characters (including newlines) and are capped at 1024 characters.
- `openvtc-core` API (breaking, listed in the CHANGELOG): `UnlockCode` / `UnlockKey`, `SecuredConfig::save`, `ProtectedConfig::save/load` (`ProtectedBinding`), `PublicConfig::legacy_logs`, `passphrase_encrypt{,_blocking}` replacing the `_v2` pair, `SecuredConfigFormat::check_unlock_code` takes the profile.

## Tests

- `openvtc-core/tests/secured_store.rs` (new; installs an in-memory credential store with write counting and fault injection): new-format round trip; legacy blob (tagged and untagged) opens, is migrated, and only the right code opens it before and after; two profiles with the same code get different salts; **write fails during migration** → legacy blob untouched, still opens, migrated next time; **write lands but does not read back** → original restored and still opens; sealed blob moved to another profile is rejected (AAD); unchanged save skips the keyring write, while changed content, a new passphrase and removing the passphrase all write; a failed write is retried, not skipped; a load clears the skip record.
- `secured_config` unit tests: right/wrong code for both formats; AAD mismatch; sealed blob round trip and stored salt; sealed blob has no shape in common with the legacy untagged parse and passes the file-store policy; damaged salt is an error, not a wrong code; fingerprint covers mode/salt/content; `key_info` serialises deterministically.
- `config/mod.rs`: salts differ per derivation, same salt reproduces the key, `UnlockKey` `Debug` is redacted, `UnlockCode` reuses its derived key.
- `protected_config`: bound blob does not open as another profile or as an export (and vice versa); legacy blob opens under any binding; config without `logs` parses.
- `loading`: the D12 fallback tests now run bound; a blob bound to another profile is refused under every key.
- `config_encryption.rs`: OPV3 round trip, wrong `info` rejected, OPV3 relabelled as OPV2 rejected, tampering; OPV2 and v1 blobs and exports still import (existing known-answer vectors kept); export carries the live protected tier, is unbound and `0600`; blocking variant parity.
- `logs`: `insert` strips bidi/ANSI/control/zero-width and caps length; `absorb` merges in time order, sanitises and keeps the newest.
- `public_config`: an old config's plaintext log moves to the protected tier and is never serialised back; `save` writes a `0600` file in a `0700` directory with the log encrypted.
- `private_file`: replaces content, `0600` over a looser existing file, failed rename leaves target intact and no temp file, failed write leaves the old file intact, symlink refused and not followed, created directory `0700`.
- `secret_buffer`: growth, edit and hand-over.

Verified locally (Rust 1.100): `cargo fmt --all --check`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`; the same with `--no-default-features`; `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets --features dev-overrides -- -D warnings`; `cargo test --workspace` and with `--no-default-features`; `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`. Not run against a real OS keyring (macOS Keychain / Secret Service) — the migration was exercised only through the in-memory store.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — no network code touched.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — the new mutexes (unlock-key cache, write-skip record) are held only for map/cache operations, never across an await.
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — no remote effects; local writes only.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — no retries added; the migration is attempted once per load.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — none touched.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — none touched.
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — no wire types changed. The on-disk envelopes are local storage, not protocol; they keep the existing snake_case/tagged shapes, and the new variant is unknown-variant-rejected by older builds by design.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — a missing/garbled salt is an error, not a fallback; the downgrade (format vs intent) gate covers the new variant; AAD mismatch fails closed.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — migration success is logged only after the read-back confirms it; failure is logged at `warn`/`error` with the reason.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — see *Migration and crash safety*: secured-blob upgrade (single replace, both versions open), `config.json` (atomic rename; old protected/log forms still read), export/report (atomic, old file intact), import (secrets before file).
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none.

## For reviewers

- `openvtc-core/src/config/secured_config.rs` — `SecuredConfig::load` / `upgrade_password_blob` (the migration) and `save` (the write skip).
- The profile-name binding decision and the downgrade story above.
- `UnlockCode`'s key cache: a wrong code's salted key is dropped (`forget_salted`), and each prompt attempt builds a new `UnlockCode`.
- Residual risk, not addressed here: a legacy (no-AAD) protected blob is still accepted, so someone with write access to `config.json` can substitute an older, pre-upgrade blob of the *same* profile (rollback). Closing that needs a monotonic counter or a "minimum format" flag in the secured blob, coordinated with the two-file write; left as a follow-up.



Closes #566, closes #569, closes #568, closes #567, closes #564, closes #570.

**Not for backport:** once a profile is unlocked by this version, 0.7 cannot open it.

title: security(config): salted unlock key, AAD, encrypted activity log, atomic writes (#602)
body:
security(config): salted unlock key, AAD, encrypted activity log, atomic writes (#602)

One storage-format change for #566, #569, #568, #567, #564 and #570.

- #566: the secured config is sealed under an Argon2id key with a random
  salt per profile (new PasswordSealed envelope, salt beside the
  ciphertext). UnlockCode now holds the code and derives against the
  stored salt; Config carries the derived UnlockKey so saves run no
  Argon2. A legacy fixed-salt blob is rewritten on its first unlock in a
  single store write that is checked before and read back after.
- #569: secured and protected blobs bind a format tag and the profile
  name as AES-GCM associated data, with a separate HKDF label per blob
  kind. Exports bind to no profile; the OPV3 passphrase envelope feeds
  info into HKDF and binds its header. Old blobs still open.
- #568: the activity log moves into the encrypted ProtectedConfig; an
  older config's plaintext log is carried across on load. Logs::insert
  sanitises and caps every message.
- #567: shared atomic_write_private (0600 temp file, fsync, rename) for
  config.json, exports, failure reports and the file secret store;
  profile directory created 0700; symlinked export targets refused.
- #564: the keyring write is skipped when the secured plaintext and its
  protection are unchanged since this process last wrote them.
- #570: SecretString/zeroizing buffers for passphrase actions, form
  buffers, start-up unlock input and the setup access token; zeroizing
  plaintext in secured_config; redacted Debug for Ticket; subtle for the
  ticket compare.

title: refactor(state_handler): split vetting_actions and persona_actions along their seams
body:
Mechanical split of the two largest `state_handler` modules into directory modules along the seams listed in #532.

**No behaviour change.** Code is moved, not rewritten. The only edits are the ones the move forces:
- `mod` declarations and `use` paths
- `pub(super)` on items a sibling module now uses (plus the fields of `SendJob`, `Presenting` and `CardJob`, which `send`/`faces` build)
- `pub(crate) use` re-exports in each `mod.rs`, so every outside path (`state_handler::vetting_actions::X`, `state_handler::persona_actions::X`) still resolves. No caller outside the two modules was edited.
- intra-doc links to items now in a sibling module get an explicit target, so `cargo doc` with `-D warnings` stays clean
- the `include_str!` fixture path in a vetting test gets one more `../`, because the file is one directory deeper
- each `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` moved beside the code it tests; fixtures shared across test modules live in a `#[cfg(test)] test_support.rs`

Test count for the `openvtc` bin: **1049 before, 1049 after** (`cargo test -p openvtc --bin openvtc -- --list`). Every test is kept; only their module paths changed.

Two commits: the first is a pure `git mv` of each file to `<name>/mod.rs`, so history follows. The second moves code out of `mod.rs`. `git diff --color-moved` and `git blame -C -C` show the moved blocks.

## Layout

### `state_handler/vetting_actions/` (was 8,733 lines)

| File | Lines | Contents |
|---|---:|---|
| `mod.rs` | 37 | module docs, `mod` declarations, re-exports |
| `words.rs` | 1,087 | display wording: grants, hidden-vetting standing, tokens, next steps, requirements (`outlook_words`, `get_tokens_words`, `community_display`, `progress_line`, …), plus their tests |
| `view_sync.rs` | 741 | `sync` and `sync_journey`, which rebuild the view model from the book, plus tests |
| `dispatch.rs` | 812 | `dispatch`, form navigation (`input`, `back`, `move_field`, `cycle`), `submit`, plus the `page`/`status`/`persist` helpers and a test |
| `send.rs` | 108 | `begin`, `abandon`, `persona_did`, `resolver`, `sign_and_send`, `spawn_send` |
| `applicant.rs` | 663 | applicant side: start/abandon an application, switch path, request a vetter, vetter directory, plus a test |
| `faces.rs` | 788 | faces at the VTA: new-face form, list/wear faces, `send_card`, `preview_refusal`, plus tests |
| `vetter.rs` | 366 | the vetter's directory profile, event-mode and resend requests, plus a test |
| `tickets.rs` | 636 | `ticket_check`, issue/mint/delete tickets, `settle_pending_tickets`, plus tests |
| `desk.rs` | 653 | vetter desk: `open_session`, `attest`, `decline`, `withdraw`, `refresh_vetter_side`, `refresh_stale_modes`, `desk_open` |
| `hidden.rs` | 396 | hidden vetting: `hidden_vetting_tick`, `ensure_hidden_vetter`, `attest_hidden`, `ask_for_challenge` |
| `pcs.rs` | 699 | PCS work at the VTA: `pcs_work_due`, `start_pcs_work`, `apply_pcs_outcome`, recovery and inbound handling |
| `jobs.rs` | 534 | `Sent`, `SendJob`, `FaceJob`, `CardJob` |
| `outcome.rs` | 831 | `VettingOutcome` and its `apply`, `sent_result`, plus tests |
| `answers.rs` | 687 | community answers, directory rows, `expire_queries`, grant checks, journey focus, plus tests |
| `test_support.rs` | 131 | shared test fixtures (hidden-vetter book, mode readings, pending ticket, first-vtc manifest) |

### `state_handler/persona_actions/` (was 4,085 lines)

| File | Lines | Contents |
|---|---:|---|
| `mod.rs` | 51 | module docs, `mod` declarations, re-exports |
| `reducer.rs` | 2,133 | `PersonaEffect`, `apply` (the reducer), `confirm_yes`, plus its tests (about 1,200 of these lines) |
| `form.rs` | 536 | `form_submit`, `release_form`, `compose_values`, editor fillers, `step`, `world_rank`, plus tests |
| `jobs.rs` | 664 | `PersonaJob`, `DISCLOSURE_PAGE`, `PersonaReadJob`, `PersonaJobRun`, re-read-after-write helpers |
| `outcome.rs` | 748 | `PersonaOutcome` and its `apply`, plus tests |
| `test_support.rs` | 52 | shared test fixtures |

## Not done here
- `persona_actions::apply` (~900 lines) and `PersonaOutcome::apply` (~420 lines) are still single functions. Splitting `PersonaAction` handling per sub-pane, as the issue suggests, means restructuring their `match` arms. That is not a move, so it is left for a follow-up.
- `VettingOutcome::apply` (~330 lines) and `dispatch` (~455 lines) are likewise moved whole.
- #533 (main page key handling) follows in a separate PR, after the config-storage PR merges.

## Verification
- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and the same with `--no-default-features`
- `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets --features dev-overrides -- -D warnings`
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`
- `cargo test --workspace`, and the same with `--no-default-features`: all pass

Closes #532

title: chore: manifests, dependency hygiene and CI hardening from the repository review
body:
One PR for four review issues. Each claim was checked against current `main` (aa9fed6), not against the commit the issues were written on.

## #544: manifest comments

- In the root `Cargo.toml`, `openvtc/Cargo.toml`, `openvtc-core/Cargo.toml` and `deny.toml`, each dependency's comment is now at most about 5 lines stating the current invariant: what it follows, what must move in lockstep, and the `cargo tree` check that proves it. The version-by-version history is gone; git history and `CHANGELOG.md` already hold it.
- Fixed the contradictions the issue lists: `dtg-credentials` ("0.11 / patch block"), `dirs` ("held at 6"), the `vta-sdk` header ("the 0.38 line"), `trust-tasks-rs` ("0.20 → 0.21"), `did-git-sign` ("floor 0.4.10 / 0.4.14"), the core dev-dep's "vta-sdk 0.56", and the conflicting histories in `deny.toml`.
- Other stale claims I found and corrected:
  - The `argon2` 0.5 duplicate comes from `pgp`, not from the mediator crates.
  - The keyring-store comments still described a per-binary store. Stores are now registered by `vta_sdk::keyring_init::install_default_store`, and keyutils is only the migration path.
- Every "one node" claim was checked with `cargo tree -i <crate> -e normal,build,dev`: dtg-credentials, trust-tasks-rs, trust-tasks-capability-client, vta-sdk, didwebvh-rs, affinidi-messaging-sdk, affinidi-tdk, dirs, vti-common, agent-names and the net-guard crates each have exactly one node.
- No dependency version or feature changed under this item.

## #538: dependency hygiene

1. **`deprecated = "allow"` removed** from `[workspace.lints.rust]`. Clippy under the default, `--no-default-features`, `dev-overrides` and `arbitrary` feature sets gives zero deprecation warnings: since #512 nothing uses the prebuilt spec modules. So no `#[allow(deprecated)]` was needed anywhere.
2. **Unused dependencies removed**, confirmed by `cargo machete`, a clean build, and cargo 1.100's own `unused_dependencies` manifest lint:
   - `openvtc`: aes-gcm, byteorder, card-backend-pcsc, hex, multibase, regex, serde_json_canonicalizer, sha2, sysinfo.
   - `openvtc`: apple-native, dbus-secret-service and windows-native keyring stores. No code references them; `vta-sdk`'s `keyring` feature pulls the same crates with the same features (`keychain` included, checked with `cargo tree -e features`). `linux-keyutils-keyring-store` stays because it is used directly.
   - `openvtc-core`: x25519-dalek.
   - **Now optional under `openpgp-card`**, because a `--no-default-features` build never uses them: `pgp` in both crates, `byteorder` in `openvtc-core`, `x25519-dalek` in `openvtc`.
   - Dropped the unused `description` / `readme` from `[workspace.package]` (cargo warned about them; both crates set their own). The workspace `version` is untouched.
3. **`sysinfo`** is now `default-features = false, features = ["system"]` (0.40.1, per `Cargo.lock`). `process_lock` refreshes only the one PID the lock file names, through `refresh_processes_specifics(ProcessesToUpdate::Some(&[pid]), …)` in a small `pid_is_alive` helper with a unit test. Before, it built a `System` over the whole process table.
4. **tokio features declared**:
   - Workspace: `macros`, `rt-multi-thread`, `signal`, `sync`, `time`.
   - Dev-dependencies add only what tests use: `net` and `io-util` for the loopback listeners, `test-util` for the paused clock.
5. **`did-git-sign` / `vgi-core` moved into `[workspace.dependencies]`**. Both crates were pinning them separately.
6. **Duplicates (dalek 2/3, rand 0.8/0.9/0.10, etc.)**: note only, as scoped. `pgp` 0.21.1 and `openpgp-card-rpgp` 0.9.1 are now published but still require `rand ^0.8` and `x25519-dalek ^2`. So a coordinated `pgp` move is possible, but it doesn't resolve the dalek/rand duplicates. This is recorded in `dependabot.yml`.
7. **`unsafe_code = "deny"`** at workspace level, with one `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` on the `libc::poll` in `openvtc/src/theme/terminal.rs`. `openvtc-core` keeps its `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`, and its test-only `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` for `env::set_var` is unchanged.

## #539: CI

- `concurrency` group `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}`, with `cancel-in-progress` only for `pull_request`. Pushes to main and release branches are never cancelled, because `nightly.yml` reads those runs.
- `timeout-minutes` on every `ci.yml` job:
  - fmt / machete: 10
  - audit / deny: 15
  - doc: 45
  - clippy, test-no-default-features, test-dev-overrides, bench, msrv: 60
  - test (3-OS): 90
  - coverage: 120
  - `verify-trust.yml` also gets 15. The other workflows already had timeouts.
- `--locked` on every cargo build/test/clippy/check/doc/bench/llvm-cov call in `ci.yml`. `publish-crates.py` already passes `--locked` to `cargo package` and `cargo publish`.
- New clippy step with `--no-default-features`, added to the existing **Clippy** job so the job name, and any required check on it, stays the same.
- The MSRV job now runs `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked`.
- New `machete` job running `cargo-machete@0.9.2` through the already-pinned `taiki-e/install-action`.
- The "Add swap" step, pasted nine times, is now a local composite action, `.github/actions/add-swap`. Every third-party action is still SHA-pinned; no new ones were added.
- `actionlint` is clean.

## #572: supply chain

1. **Advisory lists reconciled.** `deny.toml` and `.cargo/audit.toml` now carry the same IDs with the same reasons, and each file says to keep them in step. Each is dated 2026-11-15.
   - **Kept:** RUSTSEC-2023-0071 (rsa, via pgp), 2026-0173 (proc-macro-error2, dev graph only), 2026-0387 (crypto-bigint 0.5, via pgp).
   - **Pruned, because they no longer match `Cargo.lock`:** 2026-0097 (rand 0.8.8 is patched), 2024-0370, 2025-0134, 2026-0194/0195 (quick-xml is 0.41), and 2024-0436 (paste is gone; cargo-deny was warning `advisory-not-detected`).
   - **The one documented difference:** RUSTSEC-2026-0330/0331 (libcrux-kem) stay in `audit.toml` only. libcrux-kem is in `Cargo.lock` as an optional dependency of `hpke-rs-libcrux` that no enabled feature builds. cargo-audit scans the lockfile and flags it; cargo-deny checks the built graph and never sees it.
   - The stale "aes-gcm 0.10" comment is gone.
2. **verify-trust.** The action SHA is confirmed to be the `v0.29.0` tag. `version: v0.16.0` is a real but older binary release. The comment claiming they come from the same release is replaced with an accurate one: before enabling, move `version:` to the action's release in the same change, and check that the registry grants use the `github.com/...` resource form. The action and `version:` are both unchanged.
3. **Silent skip.** Commented in place: the job is not a required check yet, and once dogfooded it should fail when unconfigured. Left that way on purpose.
4. **Dependabot ignores.** Added a dated re-check note (2026-11-15) covering the three held crates, their link to the pgp-borne advisories, and the newly published `pgp` 0.21.1 / `openpgp-card-rpgp` 0.9.1.
5. **Backport token scope.** This can't be verified from the repository. Please confirm `RELEASE_TOKEN` is a fine-grained token scoped to contents + pull requests on this repo only.

## Left out

- **Coverage floor (#539):** not added. It needs a threshold agreed first.
- **The duplicates item (#538.6):** note only, as above.
- **`cargo semver-checks`:** has no `--locked` added.

## Checks run (Rust 1.100.0, macOS aarch64)

- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked --no-default-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets --locked --features dev-overrides -- -D warnings`
- `cargo clippy -p openvtc-core --all-targets --locked --no-default-features --features arbitrary -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace --locked`, the same with `--no-default-features`, and `cargo test -p openvtc --locked --features dev-overrides`
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --locked`
- `cargo +1.95.0 check --workspace --all-targets --locked` (MSRV)
- `cargo deny check`: advisories, bans, licenses and sources all ok. The remaining warnings are `multiple-versions` duplicates and two existing `license-not-encountered`.
- `cargo audit`: clean, no warnings.
- `cargo machete`: clean.
- `actionlint`: clean.

The Linux and Windows builds were not run locally; CI covers them.

Closes #544
Closes #538
Closes #539
Closes #572

title: fix(net): network and identity safety from the repository review
body:
PR 2 of the remediation plan on #589: network and identity safety.

Closes #571, closes #558, closes #573, closes #562, closes #561, closes #560, closes #559. Part of #557.

## Changes

**Agent names (#571)**
- A claim, park, resume or remove no longer caches `format!("{host}/@{name}")` as a verified name. It calls the new `Config::forget_cached_agent_name`, so the background sweep re-verifies with the full round-trip. Opening the overlay (no change) leaves a verified name alone. The now-unused `host` field on the job/outcome is removed.
- A name pulled from VTA state sync is stored unchanged, so it projects to the same record and is not pushed back. Its DID is also added to a new local-only set, `ProtectedConfig::agent_names_unverified` (serde default, skipped when empty). `cached_agent_name` returns `None` for those DIDs, the refresh targets include them, and `set_cached_agent_name` clears the mark. Marking the synced entry stale instead would have made devices push it back and forth.

**Peer-advertised answers (#558)**
- New crate-private `foreign_http::read_text_capped`: a `Content-Length` pre-check, then vta-sdk's `read_body_capped`, at `DEFAULT_MAX_FOREIGN_BODY` (2 MiB). It is used for the join-manifest fetch and the ballot-box answer. An oversize answer maps to `Unreadable`, not `Unreachable`; for a cast, resending would not change it. Tests cover declared, chunked and in-cap bodies.

**#573**
- `post_cast` uses `EndpointPolicy::public_only()`. `process_default()` honoured `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS` in release builds.
- New `display::webvh_path_tail`, built on `WebVHURL::parse_did_url` (a `did:scid` is read through `webvh_did`). `health`'s `short_tail` uses it. A path-less `did:webvh` now shows `host[:port]`, not `host%3Aport`, and a `did:key` is shown whole.
- `rebuild_apply` builds the sub-context id with `build_sub_context_id`, so it is validated and slugified. **Behaviour change:** a rebuilt `did:scid` community's placeholder id is `top/qmv` (lowercase) rather than `top/QmV`, and a path-less `did:webvh` gets its SCID token rather than its host.

**#562** `agent_name::resolve_identifier` is bounded at `IDENTIFIER_RESOLVE_TIMEOUT` (15 s) and returns `Unreachable` on timeout. That covers the relationships form, the join entry and the witness job. The join screen shows "Resolving …". The relationships form gets the bound but no live status, because its dispatch has no state sender.

**#561** `send_message_via` clones the ATM and DID out, then packs after the read guard drops, as `pickup_stored` does.

**#560**
- The four TSP discovery helpers in `config/mod.rs` share one local-mode `DIDCacheClient` (`tokio::sync::OnceCell`), so the document cache is actually used.
- The status-list client (`shared_status_client`) and the manifest client (one per `ProbePolicy`) are built once.

**#557 (part)**
- A persona's VTA-held keys are fetched concurrently (`try_join_all`). vta-sdk 0.80's DIDComm session demuxes replies by `thid` (`didcomm_session.rs`, the F5 fix), so the comment that kept these sequential is stale and has been removed. Nothing is inserted unless every key loads.
- The relationship-key fan-out is capped at 8 at once.
- Not done: loading several personas in parallel. `load_step2` threads `&mut TDK` through each persona, so that needs restructuring.

**#559** `health` resolves and probes up to 4 parties at once (`buffered`), and a party's endpoints are probed together. Progress is buffered per party and replayed in order, so the output still reads one party at a time.

## Behaviour changes (R3.6)
- A newly claimed agent name is displayed once the background sweep (≤ 5 min) has verified it. It no longer shows immediately.
- A name synced from another device is not shown until this device has verified it.
- Peer-advertised answers over 2 MiB are refused.
- No wire types or config formats changed. The new `ProtectedConfig` field is optional and omitted when empty.

## Testing
New tests: `foreign_http` (3), `display::webvh_path_tail` (2), `rebuild_apply` sub-context naming (2), `health_cmd` short-tail cases, `vta_sync::a_synced_agent_name_is_not_shown_until_verified_here`, and agent-name overlay tests (a change forgets the name; a plain listing keeps it).

Local, all exit 0: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (with and without `--no-default-features`), `cargo test --workspace` (with and without `--no-default-features`), `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets --features dev-overrides -- -D warnings`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`. Not tried against a live stack.

## Pre-merge checklist
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): the shared clients keep their existing timeouts; identifier resolution gains one
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): #561 fixed
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): the cache changes are local
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): fan-outs bounded (8 keys, 4 health parties); no retries added
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): unchanged
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): unchanged
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): none; the synced agent-name record is unchanged
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): ballot box pinned to public hosts; unverified names are not shown
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): #571
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): a forgotten name is re-verified by the next sweep
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: docs: refresh user and contributor docs from the repository review
body:
Documentation refresh from the repository review. No code changes; two `Cargo.toml` metadata edits and a LICENSE copy in each crate. No `version` field is touched.

## What changed

**#540 — command reference**
- `docs/openvtc-tool-commands.md` rewritten from `cli.rs` and the `*_cmd.rs` files: `setup` (wizard and headless `--vta-did` / `--unlock-code-file` / `--context` / `--wait`), `health` (`--vtc`, `--json`, `--recoverable`, `--allow-private-probes`), `theme {list,set,import,new,export}`, `community join`, `repo {list,clone,sign}`.
- Global options now include `--unlock-code-file`, `--monochrome` and `--invitation`; `-u/--unlock-code` is marked deprecated. `--profile` is documented as accepted before or after the subcommand (made global in #597).
- Environment variables listed in one table (none appear in `--help`); notes there are no shell completions.
- "Planned commands" removed here and in the README; the TUI section names the real main menu.

**#541 — onboarding and user guides**
- README getting-started now describes the VTA flow: setup connects to a VTA and authorises via PNM; the persona DID is created through the VTA on the first community join; headless `setup --vta-did …` and `community join` shown; `openvtc health` for checking. Self-hosted `did.jsonl`, "default mediator" and the domain prerequisite removed.
- `cargo install openvtc` added (README and `openvtc/README.md`); Windows config path corrected to `%APPDATA%\openvtc` (`dirs::config_dir()`); `dev-overrides` added to the feature table.
- `docs/multiple-didweb-same-domain.md` deleted.
- `docs/backup-restore.md` rewritten around Settings → Export Config, setup → Recover from backup, and recovery from the VTA Trust Context (`health --recoverable`, the [R] recover path and its known gaps).

title: fix(tui): user-facing bugs from the repository review
body:
PR 1 of the remediation plan on #589: the user-facing bugs, kept small enough to backport to `release/0.7`.

Closes #574, closes #563, closes #575, closes #577, closes #581, closes #583, closes #586, closes #587.

## Changes

**Unlock code length (#574) and key derivation off the render task (#563)**
- The setup wizard and backup import check the minimum length (`validate_passphrase`) before accepting a new unlock code. Every unlock path already required 8, so a shorter code locked the profile for good.
- Unlocking now uses the new `UnlockCode::for_existing`, which derives without the length check. A short code set by an earlier release therefore still opens its profile, and the user is told to set a longer one. A short code that does *not* open the profile still gets the "too short" message from #590.
- Setup sends the code to the handler (`Action::SetUnlockCode`), which derives it with `derive_passphrase_key_blocking` and then creates the account. The unused `SetProtection` action and `NavResult::SendActionThenCompleteSetup` are removed. Import runs inside `block_in_place`, so the render task keeps drawing while Argon2 runs.
- Import refuses a backup protected by an unlock code when no valid new code is given. Before, it derived a key from an empty string.

**Token Factory Reset (#575)**
- Enter on Factory Reset opens a confirmation that names the card (identifier and manufacturer) and warns when that card protects this profile. `RESET` must be typed to proceed. With no card, or more than one, nothing is offered. The card is looked up again at confirm time, and nothing is erased if it changed.

**Status colour (#577)**
- `status_style` matches failure wording anywhere in the message, case-insensitively ("couldn't", "unavailable", "not available", …). Anything else uses the plain text colour instead of success green. Moving all ~200 `status_message` sites to a typed `Status` is UX-consistency work and is left to PR 8 of the plan.

**Passphrase forms (#586)**
- Export Config has a Confirm field. Export and Change Protection report an empty, short or mismatched passphrase in the form rather than ignoring Enter, and the length-only "may not match" hint is gone. Enter on the first passphrase field moves to Confirm. The Import footer now says "import". Not done: the suggested verify-by-decrypt step after export.

**Diagnostics (#581)**
- `openvtc --setup` → `openvtc setup`. "Settings -> Import / Restore Backup" → `openvtc setup` then Restore Backup (the profile cannot load in that state), or "Settings -> Import Config" on the loading screen. "Config Protection" → "Protection".
- `--profile` is `global(true)`, so `openvtc health --profile X` (as the diagnostics print it) works.
- A new test extracts every `` `openvtc …` `` command the diagnostics emit, for each error class, and parses it with `cli()`.

**Stdout and non-terminal use (#583)**
- The `OPENVTC_CONFIG_PROFILE` notices go to stderr.
- With stdin or stdout not a terminal, the interactive path stops before the unlock prompt and lists the headless commands.

**Signals and terminal restore (#587)**
- SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP all go through the terminator (`Interrupted::OsSignal(name)` replaces `OsSigInt`). That gives them the graceful shutdown: final save, lock release, terminal restore.
- The panic hook and normal exit share `reset_terminal`, which also turns off bracketed paste and shows the cursor.
- F10 is no longer swallowed on the join DID page while it is processing. It takes effect when the in-flight resolve ends. Cancelling the resolve itself needs the join flow on the main loop (#529, PR 9).
- A user quit prints nothing. Signal and error exits explain themselves on stderr.

## Behaviour changes (R3.6)
- Status messages that are not failures are drawn in the plain text colour, not green.
- `openvtc` with stdin or stdout redirected now exits with an error instead of drawing the TUI.
- Exit messages moved to stderr, and a normal quit prints none.
- No wire types or config formats changed. `openvtc-core` gains `UnlockCode::for_existing` and `openpgp_card::card_identity` (additive).

## Testing

New tests: `cli::tests::every_command_the_diagnostics_suggest_parses`, `profile_is_accepted_before_or_after_a_subcommand`, `status::tests::failures_without_an_error_prefix_are_red`, `secured_config::tests::a_short_existing_code_still_unlocks`, an updated navigation test for `SetUnlockCode`, and updated export/import form tests (export tabs through 3 fields).

Local, all exit 0: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (with and without `--no-default-features`), `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`, `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets --features dev-overrides -- -D warnings`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`.

Not run interactively: the token reset confirmation (no card to hand), the signal paths, and the setup and import screens. They are covered only by the unit tests above and by reading the code.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no network code touched
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): local only
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retries added
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): unchanged
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): unchanged
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): none
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): a failed key derivation in setup stops before account creation rather than falling back to plaintext; token reset refuses on any doubt about the card
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): failures no longer render as success (#577); forms say why they did not submit
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): SIGTERM/SIGHUP now take the graceful path that flushes the save
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none
