title: vti-trust-task-server-v0.11.0
body:
### Build & CI

- **deps**: Enforce cargo-deny bans/sources, drop unused deps, hoist shared deps, forbid unsafe ([#2708](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2708))

* build(deps): enforce cargo-deny bans/sources, drop unused deps, hoist shared deps, forbid unsafe

  pgp, openssl only via webauthn-rs 0.5, no wildcards, and
  multiple-versions = "deny" with a skip list of today's duplicates grouped by
  cause. The two advisory ignores cargo-deny reports as not detected
  (RUSTSEC-2026-0381, RUSTSEC-2024-0436) are removed, the stale [graph]
  comment rewritten, and the yanked crypto-bigint 0.7.6 moved to 0.7.11.

  ring leaves the VTA and VTC graphs; it stays only under attest-verify.

  removed from 19 crates; deliberate ones are listed under
  [package.metadata.cargo-machete] ignored. A tier-0 "manifest hygiene" CI job
  runs cargo-machete and the lint check.

  once in [workspace.dependencies]; vta-tee inherits aws-lc-rs. The five
  crypto crates carry real minimum-patch floors, enforced by
  check-workspace-version-reqs.py.

  (check-workspace-lints.py); unsafe_code = "forbid" workspace-wide, with
  the four crates that need unsafe restating the table at "deny" and
  rewritten safely. The two missing publish = false comments are added.



### Changed

- **vta**: Decouple vta-cli-common, split key/room modules, extract vta-test-support, share reject helpers and service plumbing ([#2730](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2730))

* refactor(vta): put vta-cli-common and dialoguer behind cli-synthesis ([#2566](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2566))

  Only the `vta` binary's offline CLI modules and setup wizard use them,
  and the binary already requires `cli-synthesis`. The library — and so
  vta-enclave — no longer compiles vtc-client, ratatui, qrcode, dialoguer
  or crossterm: `cargo tree -p vta-enclave -e normal` drops from 981 to
  ~935 unique lines.

  The vti-rooms comment claimed `default-features = false` kept the host
  half out of the build; feature unification through vti-rooms-dtg (which
  verifies through `vti_rooms::authz`) turns `host` back on. Say so,
  and why it costs nothing new.

- **rooms**: Share the rooms/* handlers between hosts and run every host receive path on Spine ([#2731](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2731))

* refactor(room-host): receive every document through vti_trust_task_server::Spine

  room-host re-implemented the receive pipeline inline: size, freshness,
  validate_basic and the accepted-id claim/settle, with no spec-policy step
  and the proof verified lazily inside each handler. It now runs the shared
  Spine the VTC runs ([#2576](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2576)): the size gate holds each task to its declared
  maxDocumentBytes, the spec policy comes from
  vti_specs::schema_index::spec_policy_for, the proof is verified once over
  the document as received and bound to its issuer, DIDComm and TSP frames
  carry their authenticated sender so the spine binds it (VTI-OPS-021/093),
  and the duplicate-id record is StoreAcceptedIds (VTI-OPS-025..029).

  A host without a DID still refuses an expired document: the spine skips
  the recipient binding then, so before_proof applies the expiry check.
  A proof made by someone other than the issuer is now proofInvalid, as at
  the VTC, rather than permissionDenied.



### Performance

- **vta**: Cache compiled schemas and policies, verify once, bound sweeps and list pages ([#2713](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2713))

* perf(vta-sdk,vta-service): compile each Trust Task payload schema once ([#2622](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2622))

  trust-tasks-rs 0.37's against_schema / validate_value parse and compile the
  schema on every call. vta_sdk::schema_cache keeps the compiled validator by
  the &'static schema text's address (the same technique as trust-tasks-rs
  0.38's SchemaValidator), with the jsonschema release trust-tasks-rs 0.37 uses
  so the check and its error text are unchanged. The dispatch spine, the SDK's
  send-side check, room act, notifications, rooms, task consent, vetting and
  the VTA's per-handler payload checks use it.

  trust-tasks-rs 0.38 moves in lockstep with affinidi-tdk and the messaging
  SDK, so the bump is left to that train; this module then wraps
  SchemaValidator.

* fix(cli): operator-facing remediation strings name commands that parse

  Every error, hint and --help string that tells an operator what to run now
  names a command the current pnm / vta / cnm accepts ([#2631](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2631)): the retired

  and no longer lists the retired did-hosting-* template names ([#2635](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2635)). The

  holds ([#2632](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2632)), and `rooms prune` no longer says a prune reaches the host
  only: members' VTAs discard rungs at or below the epoch floor ([#2633](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2633)).

CI jobs install it with scripts/install-rust-toolchain.sh instead of a floating stable, so a new Rust release's lints can no longer turn main red with no code change; Dependabot proposes the next one as a PR. scripts/check-toolchain-pins.sh keeps the pin at or above the MSRV and the Dockerfiles in line.

  Clippy 1.95 is stricter than the stable CI ran in nonminimal_bool and collapsible_match: De Morgan rewrites at eleven call sites (behaviour unchanged), Option::take().map in vta-persona, and one allow on vti_voting::audit::check_order, where a match guard would fall through to later arms.

  multiple-versions = "deny" with a skip list of today's duplicates grouped by
  cause. The two advisory ignores cargo-deny reports as not detected
  (RUSTSEC-2026-0381, RUSTSEC-2024-0436) are removed, the stale [graph]
  comment rewritten, and the yanked crypto-bigint 0.7.6 moved to 0.7.11.

  [package.metadata.cargo-machete] ignored. A tier-0 "manifest hygiene" CI job

  crypto crates carry real minimum-patch floors, enforced by
  check-workspace-version-reqs.py.

  (check-workspace-lints.py); unsafe_code = "forbid" workspace-wide, with
  the four crates that need unsafe restating the table at "deny" and
  rewritten safely. The two missing publish = false comments are added.



### Performance

- **rooms**: Indexed record reads, per-room locks, commits outside the host lock, per-election ballot boxes ([#2712](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2712))

* perf(vti-common): per-bundle chunk lock and a progress bitmap apart from the plan

  A chunked transfer's lock is striped by bundle id, so one bundle's finalize
  (a whole-file hash) no longer stalls every other transfer ([#2596](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2596)). Progress
  is a bitmap row beside the immutable plan, read from a per-process cache, so

  letting it lapse left an unexpiring community administrator nobody claimed.

  permanent once the DID has proved itself with the token and claim code;
  vtc/admin/invites/revoke/0.1, and the void after five wrong claim codes,

  invitation for the same DID. The offline `vtc admin invite --did` writes the
  same provisional entry.

  Deferring the write to the claim, as passkey invitations do, would contradict
  create 0.2 item 3 and claim/finish 0.3 item 7, so the entry is still written
  at mint.

The library — and so vta-enclave — no longer compiles vtc-client, ratatui, qrcode, dialoguer or crossterm: `cargo tree -p vta-enclave -e normal` drops from 981 to ~935 unique lines. Say so, and why it costs nothing new. - **vtc**: Vtc-audit leaf crate, one regorus engine, typed error codes, trust_tasks split, AdminActor ([#2728](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2728)) * refactor(vti-common)!: move the VTC's audit-event vocabulary to a new vtc-audit leaf crate ### Documentation - Operator guides, CLI remediation strings and the crate map match the tree, checked in CI ([#2706](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2706)) * fix(cli): operator-facing remediation strings name commands that parse Every error, hint and --help string that tells an operator what to run now names a command the current pnm / vta / cnm accepts ([#2631](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2631)): the retired `pnm webvh …` / `vta webvh …` surface becomes `did-mgmt servers|dids …`, `pnm auth login` (pnm has none) becomes `pnm setup`, `pnm acl delete` takes the DID positionally, `list-domains` sits under `dids`, the backup descriptor hints no longer name `pnm backup save|restore`, and stale doc comments (`pnm passkey-enroll-token`, `vta export-mnemonic`, `cnm community info`) are corrected. A pnm and a vta test parse each remediation command through Cli::try_parse_from. The --template help is derived from vta_sdk::did_templates::BUILTIN_NAMES and no longer lists the retired did-hosting-* template names ([#2635](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2635)). The `rooms keys key-package` help gives the 14-day KeyPackage lifetime the code holds ([#2632](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2632)), and `rooms prune` no longer says a prune reaches the host only: members' VTAs discard rungs at or below the epoch floor ([#2633](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2633)). ### Fixed - **cli**: CLI and MCP operator UX sweep (confirmations, secrets off argv, JSON everywhere, room defaults, tool-level MCP errors) ([#2726](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2726)) * fix(cli): a corrupt profile is fatal, saves are atomic, one start-up for pnm and cnm, --version and completions ### Performance - **vta**: Cache compiled schemas and policies, verify once, bound sweeps and list pages ([#2713](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2713)) * perf(vta-sdk,vta-service): compile each Trust Task payload schema once ([#2622](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2622)) trust-tasks-rs 0.37's against_schema / validate_value parse and compile the schema on every call. vta_sdk::schema_cache keeps the compiled validator by the &'static schema text's address (the same technique as trust-tasks-rs 0.38's SchemaValidator), with the jsonschema release trust-tasks-rs 0.37 uses so the check and its error text are unchanged. The dispatch spine, the SDK's send-side check, room act, notifications, rooms, task consent, vetting and the VTA's per-handler payload checks use it. trust-tasks-rs 0.38 moves in lockstep with affinidi-tdk and the messaging SDK, so the bump is left to that train; this module then wraps SchemaValidator. ### Security - Invite grants, CSRF/HSTS/cookies, x5c path checks, guarded status-list fetch, vault zeroize, consent payload types ([#2710](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2710)) * security(vtc): a wallet admin invitation's entry expires with it until claimed, and goes with a revoke ([#2660](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2660)) vtc/admin/invites/create/0.2 item 3 writes a wallet invitation's administrator entry when the invitation is issued, and the code wrote it permanent: revoking the invitation (which create 0.2 says withdraws the authority it confers) or letting it lapse left an unexpiring community administrator nobody claimed. The entry is now written to expire with the invitation and recorded beside it (install::InviteGrant, keyed by jti). vtc/install/claim/finish/0.3 makes it permanent once the DID has proved itself with the token and claim code; vtc/admin/invites/revoke/0.1, and the void after five wrong claim codes, remove it (with its sessions and delegations) if it is still exactly what the invitation wrote. A lapsed or still-provisional entry no longer blocks a new invitation for the same DID. The offline `vtc admin invite --did` writes the same provisional entry. Deferring the write to the claim, as passkey invitations do, would contradict create 0.2 item 3 and claim/finish 0.3 item 7, so the entry is still written at mint.

### Build & CI

- **deps**: Enforce cargo-deny bans/sources, drop unused deps, hoist shared deps, forbid unsafe ([#2708](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2708))

* build(deps): enforce cargo-deny bans/sources, drop unused deps, hoist shared deps, forbid unsafe

  pgp, openssl only via webauthn-rs 0.5, no wildcards, and
  multiple-versions = "deny" with a skip list of today's duplicates grouped by
  cause. The two advisory ignores cargo-deny reports as not detected
  (RUSTSEC-2026-0381, RUSTSEC-2024-0436) are removed, the stale [graph]
  comment rewritten, and the yanked crypto-bigint 0.7.6 moved to 0.7.11.

  ring leaves the VTA and VTC graphs; it stays only under attest-verify.

  removed from 19 crates; deliberate ones are listed under
  [package.metadata.cargo-machete] ignored. A tier-0 "manifest hygiene" CI job
  runs cargo-machete and the lint check.

  once in [workspace.dependencies]; vta-tee inherits aws-lc-rs. The five
  crypto crates carry real minimum-patch floors, enforced by
  check-workspace-version-reqs.py.

  (check-workspace-lints.py); unsafe_code = "forbid" workspace-wide, with
  the four crates that need unsafe restating the table at "deny" and
  rewritten safely. The two missing publish = false comments are added.

The two missing publish = false comments are added. ### Changed - **vta**: Decouple vta-cli-common, split key/room modules, extract vta-test-support, share reject helpers and service plumbing ([#2730](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2730)) * refactor(vta): put vta-cli-common and dialoguer behind cli-synthesis ([#2566](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2566)) Only the `vta` binary's offline CLI modules and setup wizard use them, and the binary already requires `cli-synthesis`. The library — and so vta-enclave — no longer compiles vtc-client, ratatui, qrcode, dialoguer or crossterm: `cargo tree -p vta-enclave -e normal` drops from 981 to ~935 unique lines. Say so, and why it costs nothing new. - **rooms**: Share the rooms/* handlers between hosts and run every host receive path on Spine ([#2731](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2731)) * refactor(room-host): receive every document through vti_trust_task_server::Spine room-host re-implemented the receive pipeline inline: size, freshness, validate_basic and the accepted-id claim/settle, with no spec-policy step and the proof verified lazily inside each handler. It now runs the shared Spine the VTC runs ([#2576](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2576)): the size gate holds each task to its declared maxDocumentBytes, the spec policy comes from vti_specs::schema_index::spec_policy_for, the proof is verified once over the document as received and bound to its issuer, DIDComm and TSP frames carry their authenticated sender so the spine binds it (VTI-OPS-021/093), and the duplicate-id record is StoreAcceptedIds (VTI-OPS-025..029). The dispatch spine, the SDK's send-side check, room act, notifications, rooms, task consent, vetting and the VTA's per-handler payload checks use it. trust-tasks-rs 0.38 moves in lockstep with affinidi-tdk and the messaging SDK, so the bump is left to that train; this module then wraps SchemaValidator.

title: style: rustfmt for Rust 1.100
body:
Rust 1.100 (2026-11-09) ships a rustfmt that indents the closing line of `/*! … */` block comments. CI installs the latest stable, so the Format job has failed on `main` since cd7551e and on every PR (e.g. #597).

Formatting only: `cargo fmt --all` on 1.100.0. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean on 1.100.0, with and without `--no-default-features`.

Needs backporting so `release/0.7` PRs (including the #597 backport) pass Format.

Release notes

Sourced from serde-saphyr's releases.

2.1.1 Optimization and maintenance release

Fixed

  • Fixed 2.1.0 regression empty documents producing errors (#265). Empty document is a valid YAML document. Fix of this regression is the reason of making this release so early.

Performance improvements

  • Significantly reduced allocations when deserializing (#262), thanks @​mat-gas

2.1.0 Minor feature extension, maintenance and performance release

Added

  • Added opt-in Options::reject_tagged_field_names to catch misplaced tags on struct field names, with Error::TaggedStructFieldName diagnostics. Struct field names can only be strings; !!str is still accepted. As other tags can only be ignored, tag on a structure field name is almost for sure placed wrongly. This setting will be default in next major release.
  • Added Options::leading_zero_numbers_as_strings and Options::underscored_numbers_as_strings to preserve numeric spellings such as 0755 and 1_000 as strings in untyped values, including untagged enums and flattened fields (#225). Both default to false; direct typed parsing, explicit numeric tags, and mapping-key comparison keep their existing behavior.
  • Added Error::render_to to append diagnostics to any std::fmt::Write using RenderOptions, without collecting the complete output in an intermediate string (#221).
  • Added DuplicateKeyPolicy::PassThrough to delegate repeated explicit mapping entries to Serde visitors, matching serde_yaml's handling for structs, standard maps, and custom multimap visitors (#226). The default remains Error; merge expansion retains its precedence rules. See the README migration note for the scope of this option.

Deprecated

  • Deprecated SerializerOptions::empty_as_braces. Setting it to false emits YAML null for empty block collections without tags or anchors. These values do not round-trip into collection types. Omit the setting to keep the default true and emit [] or {}. Existing serialization behavior remains supported for compatibility.

Fixed

  • Emit empty lines in literal and folded block scalars without indentation, avoiding trailing whitespace while preserving whitespace in the string content (#249).
  • Expose the original std::io::Error from deserialization failures through std::error::Error::source(). The outer message is IO error, so error chains include the underlying cause only once. Standalone Miette, Figment, and Figment2 diagnostics retain the cause in their messages. Custom Miette formatters retain control over the complete message through MessageFormatter::format_standalone_message.
  • Avoid duplicate messages from Error::WithSnippet when following std::error::Error::source() by forwarding the wrapped error's source. Use without_snippet() to inspect the wrapped error. Alias errors retain their complete source chain, including snippet wrappers, for compatibility.

  • Added opt-in Options::reject_tagged_field_names to catch misplaced tags on struct field names, with Error::TaggedStructFieldName diagnostics. Struct field names can only be strings, !!str is still accepted. As other tags can only be ignored, tag on a structure field name is almost for sure placed wrongly. This setting will be default in next major release.
  • Added Options::leading_zero_numbers_as_strings and Options::underscored_numbers_as_strings to preserve numeric spellings such as 0755 and 1_000 as strings in untyped values, including untagged enums and flattened fields (#225). Both default to false; direct typed parsing, explicit numeric tags, and mapping-key comparison keep their existing behavior.
  • Added Error::render_to to append diagnostics to any std::fmt::Write using RenderOptions, without collecting the complete output in an intermediate string (#221).
  • Added DuplicateKeyPolicy::PassThrough to delegate repeated explicit mapping entries to Serde visitors, matching serde_yaml's handling for structs, standard maps, and custom multimap visitors (#226).
